issues.body:
## Outcome

Produce one verified v0.92.1 execution-wave creation receipt for the exact 45-child denominator defined by the merged planning package.

## Canonical authority

- `docs/milestones/v0.92.1/WP_ISSUE_WAVE_v0.92.1.yaml`
- `docs/milestones/v0.92.1/WP_EXECUTION_SPECIFICATIONS_v0.92.1.yaml#WP-01`

- `docs/milestones/v0.92.1/WP_EXECUTION_READINESS_v0.92.1.md`
- repository prerequisite #432 is merged and ancestral
- the reviewed planning package is merged and ancestral

## Scope

- create exactly the 45 number-free child issues in canonical catalog order
- preserve exact titles, dependencies, milestone, labels, execution-contract references, and existing-issue routing
- reconcile existing #51, #84, #122, #251, #261-#264, #342, and #345 without creating replacements
- reject duplicate planned IDs, operation keys, conflicting titles, missing dependencies, and extra creation slots before mutation
- after each create, read back the live issue and update an immutable partial receipt
- on interruption, resume from the first verified absent child without recreating or renumbering prior children

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exactly 45 unique child issues exist for the 45 planned creation slots
- [ ] Every child title and dependency matches the canonical merged package
- [ ] Every child has correct `version:v0.92.1` and milestone routing

- [ ] Partial failure resumes without duplicate creation or issue-number reuse
- [ ] Final live readback maps every planned ID to exactly one GitHub issue
- [ ] The retained receipt proves 45-of-45 with no missing or extra issue

## Stop conditions

Stop immediately if the reviewed planning digest changes, a planned ID maps ambiguously, a create result cannot be read back exactly, a dependency target is unresolved, or partial creation lacks an operator-reviewed recovery disposition. Created GitHub issue numbers are never deleted or recycled to hide a partial failure.

## Non-goals

- implementing child work
- deleting or recycling issue numbers
- recreating existing issues
- activating v0.93
- treating typed finish or worktree cleanup as a downstream execution dependency

issues.title: [Runtime v3] Make kernel wiring, contracts, and supervision authoritative
issues.body:
## Summary

Incorporate the 2026-08-24 structural Runtime v3 architecture review into the production kernel. Current source has strong deterministic topology and bounded supervision primitives, but validated wiring can drift from actual closure-captured channels, shutdown cancellation is broadcast rather than staged, and several declared contract/supervision invariants are not enforced.

## Required Outcome

Make the Runtime v3 kernel own and enforce its declared wiring, backpressure, determinism, lifecycle, failure propagation, health, startup, and shutdown behavior. Preserve deterministic ordering and fail-closed behavior while adding executable positive and negative proof.

## Confirmed Source Findings

1. `ComponentContext` carries no typed ports; factories can capture channels outside the validated topology. `PortSpec` relies on `type_name::<T>()` strings.
2. Shutdown cancels all components before awaiting any drain; dependency layers are unused.
3. Restart counters are lifetime-cumulative rather than intensity-window based.
4. Restart readiness timeout bypasses the component failure policy and immediately kills the kernel.
5. `Degrade` permanently removes the task without capability-loss propagation or a fatal core-set invariant.
6. Failure propagation is one-for-one although `direct_dependents()` already exists.
7. `DeterminismClass` is declared but not enforced across capability dependencies.
8. Channel metrics use a poisonable synchronous mutex on every send/receive.
9. Channel capacity and full policy are selected out of band rather than declared in the service contract.
10. Components cannot publish an alive-but-degraded health transition through `ComponentContext`; startup also ignores dependency-layer parallelism and lifecycle guarantee booleans lack failpoint proof.

## Work Slices

- **A — Authoritative wiring and contracts:** kernel-built named ports, stable type identity, contract-owned capacity/backpressure, exact topology-to-runtime binding.
- **B — Determinism and lifecycle enforcement:** reject deterministic-core dependencies on shell-only capabilities; make restart-safe/idempotent-start claims executable.
- **C — Staged lifecycle:** parallel startup by dependency layer; quiesce admission, flush checkpoints, close journals, drain telemetry, then egress under bounded per-stage deadlines.
- **D — Resilient supervision:** restart intensity windows/stability reset, readiness failures through policy, rest-for-one/one-for-all propagation, capability-loss propagation, declared fatal core set.
- **E — Health and hot-path safety:** component health reporting, dependent visibility, kernel liveness invariant, atomic non-poisoning channel metrics.

Slices A, B, and C are architectural prerequisites. D may build on A/C; E may proceed alongside B after the health/port contract is frozen. Split into child issues during design if ownership remains disjoint.

## Deliverables

- Updated Runtime v3 component, channel, contract, topology, supervisor, configuration, telemetry, and assembly surfaces.
- Versioned migration for service contracts/configuration; no silent reinterpretation of existing files.
- Architecture decision/update documenting wiring ownership, supervision strategy, shutdown stages, and compatibility boundary.
- Focused deterministic unit/integration/failpoint tests for every acceptance criterion.
- Runtime v3 soak proof covering restart intensity, dependency recovery, degraded capability propagation, and staged shutdown with continuity preservation.

## Dependencies

- Read-only input: merged WP-25 internal review packet from #313 for review/process provenance only.
- This work is independent of WP-27 #315 and must not be hidden inside its review-remediation scope.

## Owned Paths

- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/component.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/channel.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/contract.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/topology.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/supervisor.rs`
- tightly coupled Runtime v3 configuration, assembly, telemetry, tests, ADRs, and architecture proof artifacts declared during design

## Read-Only Inputs

- Current Runtime v3 ADRs, configuration, continuity, journal, checkpoint, telemetry, ingress, egress, and weather behavior outside the final approved owned-path list.
- The pasted structural review is advisory input; current repository source and executable tests remain authoritative.

## Serialization Gates

- Freeze the versioned port/contract schema before parallel child implementation.
- Do not merge supervisor propagation or staged shutdown against an unfrozen wiring contract.
- Preserve compatibility or provide an explicit migration; no mixed old/new topology authority.

## Validation And Proof

- Existing baseline: `cargo test --manifest-path adl-runtime-kernel/Cargo.toml --test kernel --test contracts --test configuration` (44 passed at source assessment).
- Negative tests: wiring mismatch, unstable/incorrect port type identity, forbidden deterministic-to-shell dependency, invalid capacity/policy, readiness failure under each policy, restart-window exhaustion and reset, dependency restart strategies, core degradation, poisoned/panicking sender isolation, non-idempotent start, restart-unsafe declaration.
- Positive tests: exact kernel-created port delivery, independent layer startup concurrency with deterministic barrier ordering, staged shutdown ordering and bounded deadlines, continuity/checkpoint flush before cancellation, health degradation/recovery propagation, atomic metric monotonicity under contention.
- Final exact-head Runtime v3 integration and soak review must find no actionable findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-1: The validated topology constructs and owns the exact runtime channels delivered by port name; factories cannot substitute closure-captured wiring, and port compatibility uses a stable governed identity rather than `type_name` text.
- AC-2: Capacity and full policy are versioned contract fields and the kernel rejects missing, ambiguous, or incompatible channel declarations before startup.
- AC-3: Deterministic-core components cannot require capabilities available only from governed nondeterministic shell providers; positive and denial tests prove enforcement.
- AC-4: Startup runs independent components concurrently by deterministic dependency layer while preserving readiness and failure semantics.
- AC-5: Shutdown is a proven staged drain: admission quiesces before checkpoint/journal flush, telemetry drains after durable state, and egress stops last, all under bounded deadlines with exact abort diagnostics.
- AC-6: Restart policy uses a bounded intensity window plus stability reset; restart-readiness failure follows the same declared policy as task failure.
- AC-7: one-for-one, rest-for-one, and one-for-all strategies have deterministic dependency-aware behavior; capability loss is propagated and declared core-component loss is fatal.
- AC-8: Components can publish bounded health/degradation/recovery state, dependents can observe capability availability, and the kernel cannot report healthy Running with no live core set.
- AC-9: Channel metrics are non-blocking/non-poisoning on the hot path and a component panic cannot cascade through metrics access.
- AC-10: `restart_safe` and `idempotent_start` are versioned enforced claims with failpoint proof; false declarations fail closed.
- AC-11: Existing Runtime v3 behavior remains covered by the full focused baseline plus new exact-head integration/soak evidence, with migration and rollback documented.

## Non-Goals

- Replacing Tokio, rewriting business components, or changing provider/model behavior.
- Treating observability alone as supervision authority.
- Silently breaking existing Runtime v3 config/contract files.
- Folding unrelated WP-27 review remediation into this kernel change.

## Rollback

Revert the versioned kernel wiring/contract migration as one coherent change, restore the previous contract schema and assembly path, and retain all new negative tests as regression evidence. Never roll back only topology validation while leaving new out-of-band wiring or supervision semantics active.

## Execution Boundary

This issue starts as architecture/design work. Before implementation, use typed C-SDLC v2 bootstrap, approve the versioned contract and migration design, bind an issue worktree under `<FastWork>/adl-worktrees`, create an issue-bound goal, and obtain exact-head review. Child issues may be created after the shared contract/design is approved; they must remain dependency-linked and must not merge into an unfrozen parent architecture.

<!-- csdlc-github-operation:runtime-v3-kernel-authority-review-20260824-v1 -->

issues.title: [v0.92][WP-22A] Repair quality-gate evidence hydration and release-credit semantics
issues.body:
## Problem

#311 / PR #466 executed and published a structurally valid v0.92 quality-gate packet, but the production matrix was not a meaningful feature audit. All 33 rows were generated as blocked because no row was hydrated into the validator's newly required accepted-evidence packet shape. The only accepted row exercised by the suite was a test-only #451 control.

This conflated `accepted evidence was not normalized into this packet` with `the feature or critical path is not implemented/proven`, then treated a vacuous 33/33 blocked report as completed WP-22 work. PR #466 merged and closed #311, so correction requires a new issue and PR.

## Required outcome

Produce a useful canonical v0.92 quality gate that reconstructs the full 13-feature plus 20-critical-path denominator from existing authoritative evidence, grants credit where evidence genuinely satisfies the contract, identifies concrete missing implementation/proof where it does not, and cannot publish an uninvestigated all-blocked matrix as completed gate execution.

## Scope

- Correct the #311 matrix generator, production validator, adversarial suite, retained gate/evidence records, blocker report, and v0.92 quality/readiness documentation.
- Build deterministic row hydration from canonical feature ownership, implementation paths, reviewed PR/merge identities, typed terminal or approved recordless closeout authority, positive/negative/integration/platform proof, and claim boundaries.
- Distinguish at least: accepted; real implementation missing; required proof missing; canonical evidence stale/non-ancestral; evidence normalization/mapping missing; planned/deferred by explicit milestone authority.
- Re-audit every one of the 33 rows against current repository and GitHub truth rather than inheriting #311's default blocked disposition.
- Preserve #311/PR #466 as immutable historical provenance while publishing an explicit corrective supersession packet.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: The production generator attempts deterministic canonical hydration for all 13 feature rows and 20 critical-path rows; it does not initialize every row to `accepted_evidence_packet_missing`.
- AC-2: Every accepted row binds exact repository, owner, implementation paths, reviewed head, PR head, merge, ancestry, required checks, positive/negative/integration/platform evidence, claim boundary, and typed or explicitly approved recordless terminal authority.
- AC-3: Every non-accepted row names the concrete missing implementation, proof, stale authority, explicit planned/deferred state, or unresolved mapping; `packet missing` alone is not treated as a product failure.
- AC-4: The validator independently recomputes the denominator and evidence bindings, rejects self-attested or cross-row/cross-repository substitutions, and fails on missing, duplicate, extra, ambiguous, or unclassified rows.
- AC-5: A completion/publication guard rejects a 100% blocked matrix when rows have not undergone evidence discovery and classification; an all-blocked outcome is allowed only when each row has independently verified concrete blockers.
- AC-6: Adversarial tests cover fabricated accepted rows, suppressed discoverable evidence, false product blockers caused only by normalization gaps, stale heads, non-ancestral merges, malformed terminal evidence, check/ruleset substitution, duplicate mappings, and vacuous all-blocked publication.
- AC-7: Corrected matrix, gate record, blocker report, validation receipt, v0.92 quality/readiness docs, and a #311 supersession note agree exactly and preserve downstream lock only for remaining concrete blockers.
- AC-8: One fresh exact-head review audits every row disposition and the discovery-completeness denominator before publication.

## Sequencing rule

Downstream issues depend on merged predecessor work only. Administrative terminal reconciliation, closeout receipts, derived-terminal records, and worktree cleanup are asynchronous bookkeeping and must not gate issue execution. Recordless or derived terminal data may be evidence inputs where semantically required, but their administrative completion is never a dependency edge.

## Non-goals

- No product feature implementation inside this issue.
- No waiver of real missing implementation or proof.
- No rewriting #311 or PR #466 history.
- No broad release ceremony, WP-23 documentation pass, cloud execution, paid runners, or unrelated C-SDLC redesign.

## Validation

- Focused production matrix generation and validation over exactly 33 rows.
- Row-discovery completeness and canonical evidence hydration tests.
- Positive controls from multiple distinct feature/critical-path families, not a single hard-coded row.
- Adversarial and vacuous-publication negative suite.
- JSON/Markdown/schema/exact-scope/diff hygiene.
- Fresh exact-head findings-first review.

issues.title: [v0.92][Runtime Security] Make lifecycle TLS authority config-only
issues.body:
## Problem

The Runtime lifecycle soak command currently accepts TLS certificate-chain, private-key, and trust-root paths as command-line inputs and then overwrites the corresponding Runtime configuration. This creates two competing authority surfaces, exposes sensitive filesystem paths through process metadata, and increases launch-time drift and operator error. Issue #268 encountered this directly when the Guardian invocation and Runtime config disagreed.

## Required outcome

Runtime TLS authority is config-only. Lifecycle and qualification commands consume the validated Runtime configuration and do not accept TLS certificate, private-key, or trust-root path flags.

## Acceptance criteria

- Remove TLS certificate-chain, private-key, and trust-root path flags from the lifecycle soak CLI.
- Load exactly one certificate chain, private key, and trust-root path from the Runtime init configuration.
- Validate the configured paths fail closed: absolute, present, regular files, distinct where required, and protected against unsafe symlink/path substitution.
- Validate private-key permissions without logging key material or sensitive path values.
- Do not overwrite TLS configuration from command arguments or environment variables.
- Update the bounded Guardian harness to place test fixture TLS paths only in its generated config, never argv.
- Add regression coverage proving the removed flags are rejected and config-only HTTPS/WSS lifecycle behavior works.
- Preserve existing Runtime restart, readiness, and lifecycle-soak behavior.
- Merge this fix before resuming the paid AWS qualification for #268.

## Validation

- Focused Rust argument/configuration tests.
- Executable Guardian lifecycle fixture using config-owned TLS paths.
- HTTPS and WSS readiness/lifecycle proof.
- Shell syntax and diff hygiene.
- Fresh exact-head implementation review.

## Non-goals

- Certificate issuance or rotation.
- Public DNS configuration.
- CloudFormation provisioning for #268.
- Any work on #269.

issues.title: [v0.92.1][planning] Refine C-SDLC v3 authority and PVF contracts
issues.body:
## Goal

Update the complete v0.92.1 C-SDLC v3 planning package so the v3 implementation track explicitly and mechanically closes the remaining audited v2 authority, proof, and coordination gaps, with a refined PVF contract.

## Required outcome

The v3 architecture, six-package execution plan, WBS, issue wave, quality gates, feature-proof coverage, ADR plan, checklist, demo/proof matrix, and handoff surfaces agree on one bounded contract covering:

1. Structurally bound design and implementation reviewer principals, typed assignment, and same-principal rejection across implementation, design review, implementation review, and publication.
2. Capability-matrix-driven automatic invalidation of every dependent approval, review, publication, readiness, and terminal authority after substantive mutation.
3. Exact changed-path equality across immutable base-to-candidate commits plus staged, unstaged, and untracked state; caller-selected scope subsets cannot hide extra changes.
4. PVF expected test/case identifiers and exact expected, selected, passed, failed, ignored, and skipped denominators; zero, missing, extra, renamed, filtered, or ignored cases fail closed.
5. Typed preparation-versus-bound execution evidence, so preparation-only validators cannot satisfy implementation or release proof.
6. Typed execution hold/release authority with exact issue, generation, digest, actor, reason, allowed recovery operations, and audit evidence.
7. Intentional-deletion-aware deliverables and migration/audit provenance without reopening v0.92 scope.
8. One provenance-bound v3 executable, complete v2 parity/canary evidence, operator-approved cutover, and separate retirement.

## Scope

- `docs/milestones/v0.92.1/**` C-SDLC v3 planning, proof, quality, ADR, issue-wave, and handoff surfaces.
- `docs/planning/ADL_FEATURE_LIST.md` only where C-SDLC v3/PVF milestone truth must be synchronized.
- `csdlc-v3/README.md` only to reference the refined planning authority; no v3 implementation.
- Issue-owned C-SDLC lifecycle, preparation, and evidence paths.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every audited gap has one owning v3 package, acceptance criterion, proving PVF lane, negative fixture, and stop condition.
2. V3-A freezes reviewer principal, invalidation, execution-hold, exact-scope, intentional-deletion, and PVF evidence schemas before implementation packages begin.
3. V3-D cannot claim planning readiness from preparation-only evidence, ambiguous test selectors, or incomplete scope.
4. V3-E proves execution receipts against literal expected case sets and exact counts, then binds exact review/publication/finish authority to the complete immutable candidate scope.
5. V3-F parity and cutover reject any missing v2 journey, stale audit provenance, unexercised recovery path, or operator approval gap.
6. The full canonical v0.92.1 planning package remains internally consistent and validates with focused documentation/YAML/link/path checks.
7. No v0.92 implementation issue is reopened or expanded, and no C-SDLC v3 product code is implemented in this planning issue.

## PVF refinement boundary

PVF must distinguish planned lanes, preparation evidence, bound execution evidence, deferred CI evidence, and release evidence. Exit status alone is never sufficient. Each proving receipt binds the executable/argv, platform and runner identity, immutable source revision, expected case IDs, observed case IDs and counts, artifacts and digests, redaction/path hygiene, duration, and disposition. Typed wrappers are allowed only when their schema and expected-set equality are themselves governed and tested.

## Non-goals

- Fixing or expanding v0.92.
- Implementing C-SDLC v3.
- Reopening closed v2 defects #369, #417, #418, or #421.
- Creating the six v3 implementation issues before WP-01.
- Cutting over from or deleting v2.

## Validation

- Parse every touched YAML/JSON contract.
- Validate the complete canonical v0.92.1 documentation denominator and relative links.
- Mechanically map every audit requirement to exactly one owning package and at least one proving/negative PVF case.
- Reject omitted exact-scope, denominator, reviewer-independence, invalidation, hold, preparation/bound separation, or cutover requirements.
- Run `git diff --check` over the exact candidate range.
- Obtain bounded independent review before publication.

Part of the v0.92.1 planning track established by #431. Issue creation remains planning authority only.

issues.title: [Tooling] Bridge fresh subagent review identity into typed design approval
issues.body:
## Problem

The required pre-bind design review can complete through the Codex subagent interface, but typed C-SDLC v2 `csdlc-edit approve-design` requires the reviewer field to be a canonical fresh-session UUID. The collaboration interface exposes only a task identity such as `/root/issue450_design_review_v3`; the reviewer runtime also reports that its canonical session UUID is unavailable. This leaves a passed independent review impossible to record without inventing provenance.

## Safe reproduction

1. Initialize an issue with a current design digest.
2. Run an independent read-only subagent review and receive PASS.
3. Submit `csdlc-edit approve-design` with the truthful subagent task identity.
4. Observe: `csdlc-edit: design reviewer must be a canonical fresh-session UUID` and `csdlc.error.v1 code=invalid_input`.
5. Query the subagent for its canonical UUID; it reports that only its task identifier is available.

Observed on issue #450 at design digest `3e1683199c6560ddaf4ca2a05157a75ce86c6d473b7b374a913e1250a413f790`. No credentials, response bodies, or #446 state are included.

## Expected

Provide a trustworthy bridge: either expose the canonical fresh-session UUID in subagent metadata/results, or let typed approval consume a signed/typed review receipt whose provenance resolves to that UUID. Do not weaken the fresh-review requirement or accept arbitrary reviewer strings.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fresh subagent review can produce typed reviewer provenance accepted by `csdlc-edit approve-design`.
- The approval owner still rejects fabricated, stale, or non-fresh reviewer identity.
- A focused integration test covers the Codex subagent-to-C-SDLC approval path.
- Diagnostics state how an operator obtains the required identifier without inspecting secrets or internal databases.

## Workaround status

No truthful workaround is currently available through the exposed interfaces; #450 remains at the design-approval gate despite a PASS review.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Fix csdlc-install regular-file selector false rejection
issues.body:
## Problem

At repository HEAD `aa36a828793366f92d0d9e16247bd3fb1cce7878`, the installed typed v2 resolver rejects the tracked generation selector with `tracked generation selector must be a regular file, not a symlink`, even though both the filesystem and Git identify it as a regular tracked blob. This blocks the mandatory generation-resolution preflight for issue #450 and other typed lifecycle work.

## Reproduction

From `/Users/daniel/git/agent-design-language` on clean tracked `main`:

```sh
.adl/bin/csdlc-v2/csdlc-install resolve --repo agent-logic/agent-design-language --issue 450
ls -l csdlc-v2/operator/generation-selector.json
git ls-tree HEAD csdlc-v2/operator/generation-selector.json
readlink csdlc-v2/operator/generation-selector.json
```

Observed resolver result:

```text
tracked generation selector must be a regular file, not a symlink
```

Observed selector evidence:

- `ls -l` reports `-rw-r--r--`, size 123 bytes.
- `git ls-tree` reports mode `100644`, blob `a30bcd2a739edadd776e71ca3219381b1e382080`.
- `readlink` produces no target.
- `git status --short -- csdlc-v2/operator/generation-selector.json` is empty.

The split typed GitHub reader remains functional, so this is specifically a generation-selector resolution failure, not general binary absence.

## Required outcome

`csdlc-install resolve` must correctly accept the canonical tracked regular selector while continuing to fail closed for symlinks, non-regular files, repository escape, untracked replacement, and selector digest drift.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The exact regular-file fixture above resolves the selected generation successfully.
2. A genuine symlink selector is rejected with the existing fail-closed classification.
3. Directory, FIFO/device where supported, missing-file, repository-escape, untracked replacement, mode drift, and content/digest drift fixtures fail deterministically.
4. Path inspection handles canonical repository roots and macOS filesystem semantics without misclassifying a regular file.
5. The result reports the selector path, tracked mode, selected generation, and verified digest without exposing credentials or unrelated filesystem state.
6. Focused resolver tests reproduce the current false rejection before the fix and pass afterward.

## Owned scope

- `csdlc-install` generation-selector path/type validation
- focused resolver fixtures and tests
- bounded operator documentation only if the contract changes

## Non-goals

No weakening of symlink/path-escape protections, no raw GitHub fallback, no lifecycle state repair, no mutation of #446 or #450 product scope, and no broad installer redesign.

issues.title: [v0.92][Runtime] Compose the production birthday and witness activation path
issues.body:
## Problem

The Runtime contains identity, continuity, birthday-decision, capability, cognitive-profile, adaptive-learning, Memory Palace, and birth-witness contracts, but they are not composed into one live production activation path. Runtime startup currently validates/configures a birth-witness owner; that is not a birthday transaction. Contract tests and the former bounded demo packet do not prove a resident becomes ready, is evaluated, receives a unique birthday decision, and produces a validated witness receipt through the executing Runtime.

## Required outcome

After #446 and the parallel Runtime integration foundations #448-#450 are complete, compose their verified outputs into the first production birthday/witness path with deterministic denial before readiness, exactly-once success, durable lineage, and restart-safe continuation. Re-run the prior Runtime feature-wiring audit against the merged production tree and prove every required feature is genuinely reachable from a live resident cycle.

## Dependencies

- #446 — ACC-governed resident tool execution
- #448 — production capability envelope and governed cognitive profile
- #449 — production governed Adaptive Learning
- #450 — Memory Palace production authority convergence

All four dependencies must be terminal, canonical, ancestral, and consumed at their reviewed revisions before this issue can claim successful activation. Preparation and interface review may proceed while they execute.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An actual Runtime resident—not a fixture, benchmark, metadata row, or demo-only process—progresses through verified identity and continuity, authoritative Memory Palace grounding, governed capability/profile construction, governed evaluation/adaptation, and readiness evaluation.
2. Before every prerequisite is present and current, `decide_birthday` denies activation and no birth-witness packet or success receipt is emitted. Ordinary startup, wake, restore, copied state, and process launch are explicit negative cases.
3. Once all prerequisites pass, the Runtime invokes the configured birth-witness owner, creates and validates the witness packet, and emits one durable birthday receipt bound to exact identity root, continuity head, resident cycle, Memory Palace binding, capability envelope, cognitive-profile revision, adaptive history, ACC/tool-authority state, policy, witnesses, implementation revision, and timestamp authority.
4. The birthday is exactly once for an identity lineage. Duplicate execution, restart, retry, concurrent request, stale candidate, copied state, rollback, replay, and conflicting witness attempts fail closed without a second birthday.
5. Rehydration restores the complete post-birthday lineage and deterministically continues resident work without re-running activation or losing governed authorities.
6. Negative proof covers missing/mismatched capability, stale profile, incomplete adaptive history, Memory Palace divergence, missing or invalid ACC binding, missing witness authority, forged/duplicate witness, invalid continuity, rollback, and incomplete evidence.
7. Focused production-path integration proof exercises denial-before-readiness, one successful birthday/witness transaction, durable restart, duplicate denial, and post-restore useful resident continuation. Individual unit suites are necessary but insufficient.
8. Retained evidence is redacted, exact-revision-bound, schema-valid, and suitable for #311 quality-gate consumption. No private memory/profile/provider/prompt content is published.
9. Update `docs/planning/ADL_FEATURE_LIST.md` and canonical v0.92 birthday/quality-gate documents so the first true birthday is marked complete only when this exact production proof is accepted.
10. Repeat the earlier feature-to-Runtime audit against the merged #446/#448-#450 tree. For identity, continuity, birthday decision, birth witness, Memory Palace, capability envelope, governed cognitive profile, Adaptive Learning, and ACC/tool authority, retain source-grounded evidence showing the feature is constructed, consumed, and behaviorally exercised through the production resident path. Any surface that remains library-only, fixture-only, metadata-only, documentation-only, or unreachable blocks completion.

## Likely surfaces

- Runtime-kernel activation/assembly wiring under `adl-runtime-kernel/src/`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/birthday.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/birth_witness.rs`

issues.title: [v0.92][Runtime] Wire ACC-governed tool execution into resident-agent cycles
issues.body:
## Goal

Wire ACC into the long-lived Runtime resident execution path so an agent's proposed tool action is compiled, authorized, gated, executed or denied, and recorded by the Runtime rather than by a benchmark CLI.

## Context

Issue #268 owns deployment, setup, and qualification of six resident agents on AWS. It does not own this Runtime implementation. Current #268 tooling drives `uts_benchmark_runner.py`, which invokes the provider adapter directly, while the former governed UTS+ACC demo lane was retired with the obsolete external demo surface in #5347. The underlying UTS compiler, ACC, Freedom Gate, and governed-executor libraries remain.

The production gap is that `adl/src/long_lived_agent.rs` runs resident workflow cycles but does not parse resident tool proposals or route them through ACC. `adl-runtime/src/resident_agent.rs` currently represents admission metadata and lacks a typed, enforced tool-authority binding. Per-resident tool authority in #268 is therefore checkpoint metadata, not Runtime enforcement.

## Required outcome

- Parse exactly one typed UTS tool proposal from an actual resident provider response.
- Bind the proposal to typed resident identity, role, allowed tools, and tool-authority reference/digest loaded by the Runtime.
- Compile UTS to ACC using production registry and policy context, then evaluate the Freedom Gate.
- Dispatch approved actions through a sealed governed adapter interface; models must never directly actuate tools.
- Deny authority mismatches, compiler failures, gate failures, unsupported adapters, and malformed or multiple proposals fail-closed.
- Persist a redacted terminal receipt for every proposal, binding the resident, proposal digest, ACC contract, gate decision, adapter outcome, Runtime cycle, and checkpoint lineage.
- Keep the fixture dispatcher confined to tests/demos and provide a minimal harmless Runtime adapter for proving the production path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A long-lived Runtime resident response containing an authorized proposal produces a Runtime-owned ACC contract, Freedom Gate decision, governed adapter result, and retained receipt.
2. Missing or mismatched authority, unauthorized tools, malformed/multiple proposals, gate denial, and unsupported adapters are denied with terminal redacted receipts and no actuation.
3. Resident specifications carry typed tool-authority identity/ref/digest and validation rejects incomplete or inconsistent bindings.
4. Tests cover allowed execution, compiler denial, authority mismatch, gate denial, unsupported adapter, receipt redaction, and an integration cycle using an actual Runtime provider response.
5. The implementation does not restore the retired #5347 demo and does not use benchmark success as Runtime proof.

## Non-goals

- AWS qualification or deployment owned by #268.
- Issue #269.
- Arbitrary shell, process, filesystem, or network authority.
- A broad provider or executor rewrite.

## Likely surfaces

- `adl-runtime/src/resident_agent.rs`
- `adl/src/uts_acc_compiler*`

issues.title: [v0.92.1][repository] Remove all tracked .adl paths and relocate required policy authority
issues.body:
## Summary

Make `.adl/**` strictly local-only by removing every currently tracked `.adl` path from the Git index and preventing future additions. Eliminate every repository dependency on `.adl/**`. Preserve required repository authority—especially the worktree placement policy—by relocating it to an explicit tracked path outside `.adl` and updating every consumer before the old path is removed.

## Current Evidence

The repository already ignores `.adl/`, but legacy tracked entries remain. They include planning/review notes, session handoffs, logs, one retained task card, provider-probe disposition, and `.adl/worktree-policy.json`. Because Git continues tracking ignored paths and tooling consumes at least the policy file, the current boundary is incomplete.

## Required Outcome

At the implementation head, `git ls-files .adl` returns an empty exact denominator and no tracked source, build, test, Runtime, C-SDLC, documentation, policy, CI, or release surface reads or requires any `.adl/**` path. Local `.adl` content may exist only as non-authoritative operator-local state. CI rejects future tracking or dependency on `.adl/**`.

## Required Work

1. Inventory the exact pre-change `git ls-files .adl` denominator and every tracked reference to `.adl/`; classify each path/reference as relocatable authority, retained provenance to move outside `.adl`, removable residue, or forbidden dependency.
2. Relocate `.adl/worktree-policy.json` to a reviewed tracked policy location outside `.adl` and update bind/install/doctor/tooling consumers and documentation atomically.
3. Relocate any genuinely required historical/provenance documents outside `.adl`; do not publish secrets, raw logs, local evidence, or machine-specific state.
4. Remove every remaining `.adl/**` entry from the Git index while preserving operator-local files where appropriate.
5. Remove every repository dependency on `.adl/**`, including examples, tests, scripts, docs, CI, schemas, manifests, and fallback lookup paths.
6. Keep the root `.gitignore` rule for `.adl/` and add focused guards that fail when `git ls-files .adl` is non-empty or tracked repository content introduces an authoritative `.adl/` dependency.
7. Verify fresh-checkout C-SDLC worktree binding enforces the relocated policy without creating or reading `.adl` authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-1: Exact pre-change tracked-path and reference inventories are retained as redacted migration evidence with one disposition per path/reference.
- AC-2: `git ls-files .adl` produces zero paths at the implementation head and in a fresh checkout.
- AC-3: A repository-wide tracked-source scan proves no source, script, test, documentation, CI, schema, manifest, policy, or fallback lookup depends on `.adl/**`.
- AC-4: The worktree policy has one canonical tracked location outside `.adl`; all consumers use it and reject an invalid worktree parent exactly as before.
- AC-5: `.gitignore` continues to exclude `.adl/`, and deterministic guards reject reintroduction of tracked `.adl` files or dependencies.
- AC-6: No credential, local provider output, raw log, private evidence, machine path, or operator-only state is promoted into tracked replacement surfaces.
- AC-7: Focused bind/doctor/install/path-policy tests, exact zero denominators, fresh-checkout proof, strict diff hygiene, and an independent exact-head review pass.

## Owned Scope

- Current tracked `.adl/**` paths, for migration/removal only
- All exact tracked references that currently depend on `.adl/**`
- New canonical tracked policy/provenance locations outside `.adl`
- Exact C-SDLC consumers and focused tests resolving the relocated policy
- `.gitignore` and focused tracked-path/dependency guards
- Issue-owned lifecycle and evidence paths outside `.adl`

## Non-Goals

- Deleting operator-local `.adl` content indiscriminately
- Treating local `.adl` content as fallback authority
- Moving `.csdlc/**` lifecycle authority
- Redesigning worktree placement policy
- Broad documentation cleanup unrelated to `.adl` removal
- Publishing local logs, credentials, provider output, or private session material

## Validation

Require exact zero-output proof for both tracked `.adl` paths and authoritative tracked references, fresh-checkout policy resolution, allowed FastWork bind behavior, rejected non-FastWork bind behavior, focused path-policy tests, secret/path redaction checks, and `git diff --check`. Broad Runtime tests are unnecessary unless implementation changes Runtime behavior.

## Dependency and Sequencing

This is a v0.92.1 repository/tooling migration. It must land before v0.92.1 planning or execution relies on new `.adl` documents. Existing local `.adl` files remain local-only and non-authoritative throughout.

- #374 PR #378
- #401 PR #402

Contradictory terminal precedence / no truthful materialization yet:

- #248 live closed-by-merged authority points to PR #247, while retained local publication evidence points to PR #249. Do not falsely materialize PR #249 as merged or silently choose between them.

Historical source scan:

- #204 and #211 have only initialized historical records and no publication/terminal evidence.
- #207/#266/#267/#373/#374/#401 have no `.csdlc/issues/<issue>/index.json` in `git log --all`.
- #248 has a published historical record for PR #249, conflicting with live merged PR #247.

## Required outcome

Implement a typed, audited recovery/classification path for already-merged closeout authority when no source issue projection exists at the merged PR head, without inventing implementation/card proof or weakening ordinary publication/terminal guards.

The path must support:

1. Recordless/no-projection classification for merged PR closeout candidates, naming exact issue, repository, PR, head SHA, merge SHA, issue state, PR state, and missing projection evidence.
2. Safe terminal receipt materialization only when a typed request supplies enough exact live GitHub authority and retained evidence to reconstruct minimal closeout truth without pretending normal lifecycle cards existed.
3. Explicit fail-closed contradictory-precedence classification for #248.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: A typed request requires issue, exact repository, exact merged PR, expected head SHA, merge SHA, actor, reason, token source, and a declared recovery mode: `recordless_terminal` or `classify_only`.
- AC-2: The route proves live GitHub issue is closed by the exact merged PR, the PR is merged, head SHA and merge SHA match, and the PR body contains closing authority for the exact issue.
- AC-3: The route refuses open issues, open/unmerged PRs, wrong repository, wrong issue linkage, wrong head SHA, wrong merge SHA, ambiguous closing PRs, missing token source, and any existing contradictory publication/terminal evidence.
- AC-4: The route never mutates product files, never edits GitHub state, never rewrites historical issue/card records, and never claims implementation/review evidence that is absent.
- AC-5: #248 is rejected or classified with explicit contradictory precedence between PR #247 and PR #249; no merged closeout receipt is produced until precedence is resolved.
- AC-6: #204/#207/#211/#266/#267/#373/#374/#401 produce either safe recordless terminal receipts or machine-readable fail-closed no-projection blocker results, with exact evidence and no synthesized lifecycle cards.
- AC-7: Positive tests cover a recordless closed-by-merged issue with exact PR evidence and no issue index at PR head.
- AC-8: Negative tests cover #248-style contradictory publication precedence, no issue closing keyword, wrong head SHA, wrong merge SHA, wrong repository, unmerged PR, and ambiguous multiple closing PRs.
- AC-9: The v0.92 closeout sweep can rerun after this fix and leave either 92/92 receipts or a retained blocker list containing only irreducible contradictory cases.

## Non-goals

- No raw GitHub writes.
- No manual lifecycle/card synthesis.
- No product implementation changes.
- No weakening of ordinary active-issue publication requirements.
- No treating `part_of` checkpoint PRs as terminal closing authority.
- No force cleanup of unrelated dirty worktrees.

## Validation

Focused Rust tests for the new typed recovery/classification route, plus a retained live dry-run over the 9 residual v0.92 issues before applying any eligible recordless closeouts.

## Stop condition

If the safe route cannot distinguish true closing PR authority from checkpoint/part-of/contradictory authority, fail closed and retain blocker evidence instead of materializing closeout.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Accept intentional deletion deliverables during readiness validation
issues.body:
## Problem

C-SDLC v2 readiness treats an intentionally deleted test path in exact typed scope as a required-present validator target. This makes truthful candidate-scope parity incompatible with doctor/validate readiness.

## Exact reproduction

Issue #414 is implemented at generation 39, digest `db2a393df52a64cf8f25e0743352516c178da6539f2f511b69ed8c04a7ea8a4e`, immutable branch HEAD `6108d93b8`. Its candidate intentionally deletes the rejected parallel authority path `adl-runtime/tests/resident_shepherd_spot_continuity.rs`. Fresh exact-head review R21 required that deletion to remain explicit in STP deliverables and SPP affected areas so the complete candidate scope is reviewable.

`csdlc-doctor --repo /Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-414-resident-shepherd-spot-continuity --issue 414` and `csdlc-validate --root /Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-414-resident-shepherd-spot-continuity issue --issue 414` fail with:

```text
validator_target_missing: required validator deliverable is unavailable: adl-runtime/tests/resident_shepherd_spot_continuity.rs
```

The direct implementation is `csdlc-v2/src/cards.rs:2770-2785`: every deliverable classified by `required_validator_deliverable` must exist, be deferred, or be a selected target. There is no representation for an intentional deletion that remains in exact candidate scope.

## Expected behavior

Provide a typed, fail-closed way to declare and validate an intentional deletion deliverable. It must preserve exact STP/SPP/review scope, verify that the path is an actual deletion relative to the governed base, and must not let a missing or mistyped required validator masquerade as a deletion.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A typed intentional-deletion entry can remain in exact affected-area/deliverable/review scope without requiring the deleted file to exist.
2. The validator proves the path existed at the governed base and is deleted in the exact candidate; absent, renamed, untracked, or unrelated missing paths still fail closed.
3. Ordinary test/validator deliverables retain current required-present behavior.
4. Focused positive and adversarial regressions cover #414-style deleted tests plus false deletion claims.
5. No weakening of exact-head review, publication, or topology authority.

## Scope

- `csdlc-v2/src/cards.rs` readiness classification
- the smallest typed card/schema representation needed for intentional deletions
- focused C-SDLC v2 regression tests

## Non-goals

Do not implement or alter #414 product code, evidence, design, publication, AWS work, or #268/#269. Do not remove deleted paths from exact review scope and do not treat arbitrary missing files as acceptable.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC policy] Permit audited gh break-glass during confirmed typed regressions
issues.body:
## Problem

The repository correctly requires typed C-SDLC v2 owners for covered GitHub lifecycle writes, but it has no bounded exception when a confirmed regression in that same typed control plane blocks delivery. This can turn a tooling defect into an indefinite delivery stop even after the operator explicitly authorizes a safe, reconcilable fallback.

## Required outcome

Define a narrow, fail-closed raw `gh` break-glass policy. Typed v2 remains the default and the exception is available only when a reproducible tooling regression is durably tracked and the operator explicitly authorizes one exact repository, issue or PR, and operation. Require exact-head/worktree evidence, the smallest non-destructive command, secret-safe execution, and an append-only local receipt containing the command class, targets, result, and redaction statement. Require typed reconciliation before any later lifecycle claim or finish.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Root operator policy identifies the exact prerequisites for invoking the exception and preserves typed v2 as default authority.
2. Allowed operations are narrowly enumerated; merge, finish, cleanup, deletion, force operations, and other destructive mutations remain denied by default.
3. Every invocation requires explicit operator authorization naming repository, target, and operation plus a durable regression issue and reproducible failure evidence.
4. An append-only local receipt records timestamp, actor, repository, issue or PR, exact head/worktree evidence, command class and redacted argv, result, regression issue, authorization text reference, reconciliation requirement, and excludes credentials or sensitive bodies.
5. Subsequent lifecycle claims and `csdlc-finish` remain blocked until typed state is reconciled with the remote mutation.
6. Focused documentation/contract validation proves the policy is present, internally consistent, and does not create a general raw-`gh` bypass.

## Non-goals

- Replacing or weakening typed C-SDLC v2.
- Allowing silent merge, finish, cleanup, deletion, force-push, token output, or broad repository administration.
- Using the exception before this policy is reviewed and merged.
- Mutating #414, #268, #269, or AWS as part of this issue.

## Scope

- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/tooling/SESSION_COORDINATION_AND_ROOT_CHECKOUT_POLICY.md` only if needed to locate receipt/reconciliation ownership
- focused contract validation under an existing appropriate docs/tooling test surface

issues.title: [v0.92][runtime-v3][integration] Wire resident Shepherd continuity into Spot reclamation
issues.body:
## Outcome

Bridge multiple distinct resident CPU-local Shepherd agents into the existing Runtime v2 lifecycle, snapshot, lineage, invariant, duplicate-denial, and rehydration authority so a confirmed Spot interruption dehydrates the complete admitted population and replacement capacity restores the exact population before admission reopens. This is a hard prerequisite for #256, #341, and #268.

## Existing authority reused unchanged

- Reuse the existing Runtime v2 lifecycle states and the quiescent/suspended/dormant custody path.
- Reuse `RuntimeV2SnapshotManifest`, `RuntimeV2RehydrationReport`, exact-population validation, checksum/invariant gates, lineage, sequence advancement, duplicate denial, and wake refusal.
- Reuse existing long-lived-agent continuity capsules and signed LiveContinuity checkpoint/restore authority.
- Do not introduce a new lifecycle state, snapshot schema, lineage model, or recovery system.

## Required proof shape

- Run multiple distinct resident CPU-local Shepherd agents backed by pinned local model/configuration identities, including Ollama `llama3.1:8b` Q4.
- Use one active Ollama worker at a time, conservative contexts, and no concurrent compilation.
- Every resident admits and performs useful bounded work before interruption; sentinel-only output is non-proving.
- A confirmed IMDS Spot interruption closes admission, traverses existing custody, and dehydrates every admitted resident atomically with kernel/ingress continuity within the deadline.
- Signed continuity is retained on a dedicated Runtime volume distinct from Cargo, target, sccache, and build caches.
- Replacement validates exact identity, lifecycle state, sequence, predecessor, state digest, model artifact digest, quantization, configuration digest, population completeness, rollback/tamper resistance, and no duplicate or missing activation before admission.
- Every restored resident performs deterministic next useful work.
- Operator-observable/control status covers admission, lifecycle, checkpoint, restore, resident population, and task result without private-state authority.
- Retain cold/warm latency, peak RSS, memory headroom, task-result digests, and model/configuration digests against exact `r7i.2xlarge` capacity: 8 vCPU and 64 GiB.
- An optional bounded call to a large external model may be observed separately, but it is never required for admission, local useful work, dehydration, rehydration, deterministic resume, or pass/fail.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Nonzero complete resident population is dehydrated exactly once with kernel/ingress continuity.
2. Rehydration restores every exact ID/state/sequence/predecessor/model/configuration digest before admission, with no duplicate or missing agent.
3. Missing, tampered, rollback, duplicate, partial, substituted, oversized, busy, and deadline-expired cases fail closed.
4. Multiple pinned CPU-local residents including `llama3.1:8b` Q4 perform useful work before and after recovery within 8 vCPU/64 GiB with headroom.
5. Existing Runtime v2 lifecycle/snapshot/rehydration authority remains the sole recovery authority.
6. Focused tests, real CPU receipt, fresh exact-head review, CI, merge, typed finish, canonical cache, and ancestry complete before consumers proceed.

## Bounded scope

Resident adapter, additive Runtime registration, focused resident/Spot continuity test, lifecycle-soak bridge, minimum IMDS/retained-volume runner contract, CPU habitability runner, and issue-local lifecycle/evidence. Runtime v2 lifecycle/snapshot/types remain read-only unless a concrete compile-time adapter need receives fresh review.

## Non-goals

No new recovery system, GPU, model-weight/prompt/secret serialization, paid #268 launch, On-Demand fallback, #269 mutation, or external-model dependency.

## Graph

`#414 -> #256`; `#414 -> #341`; `#266 + #267 + #414 + #415 -> #268`; #414 blocks those consumers until terminal/canonical/ancestral.

Fresh review passed exact commit `14c6771d1d7710423bd14f371e50daf00fa903ac`; typed review recording produced generation 11; typed republish produced PR head `757462d1e2267128189f6e0a2ea2ddd4d01dce8d`, generation 12, and renewed CI passed.

## Exact cause evidence

Canonical publication evidence records revision `git-blake3:14c6771d1d7710423bd14f371e50daf00fa903ac:...`, the reviewed pre-publication commit. `finish.rs::validate_publication_head_lineage_in_repo` parses that revision as `published_head`, then reads `14c6771d:.csdlc/issues/349/index.json` and requires its review to equal the current canonical review. But that historical pre-review/recovery commit necessarily has `review=null`; the exact current review first exists in the later typed review-record and republished metadata commit. Direct comparison: historical issue/repository equal current; historical review null; current review is the fresh completed review; equality false. Meanwhile `757462d1:.csdlc/issues/349/index.json` contains the exact canonical review object and the only changed paths from 14c6771d to 757462d1 are governed #349 lifecycle metadata.

## Required outcome

Make typed republish record or finish validate the correct publication metadata anchor so a supported recover-review -> fresh review -> republish sequence can finish without raw merge, hand editing, or an infinite recovery loop. Preserve exact reviewed-substantive ancestry and metadata-only governance checks.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A supported post-publication recovery, fresh review, and typed republish records an anchor whose historical issue index contains the canonical completed review.
2. Finish validates exact PR head, reviewed substantive ancestry, governed metadata-only drift, and equal canonical review evidence.
3. Pre-review or review-null publication anchors fail closed with a precise diagnostic or are normalized by the typed publication owner.
4. A regression reproduces #349's sequence and reaches terminal finish only when the republished commit retains matching review evidence.
5. No raw merge fallback and no weakening of review, CI, linkage, or ancestry gates.

## Current safe handling

PR #352 is open with renewed required CI green. Do not raw merge or repeat recover/republish; preserve it pending a supported exact reconciliation.

However, no sealed Observatory consumer projection cross-binds those fields to the #272 cut, and the committed inclusive deadline is not retained in the published result. #274 cannot accept caller-provided replacements without manufacturing authority, and its scope explicitly keeps #272/#203 contracts read-only.

## Required outcome

Provide one sealed, fail-closed authenticated Observatory authority projection/API that cross-binds a terminal #272 `VerifiedServingAuthorityCut` to the exact committed authority operation, publishing trust-domain/polis identity, lineage, quorum signer-set evidence, operation identity, and committed inclusive deadline/canonical time truth needed by #274.

1. The projection is obtainable only from replicated, published authority plus the exact verified #272 cut; callers cannot construct or substitute its fields.
2. It binds trust-domain, polis, lineage, operation ID, committed log/foundation generation, OwnerCommit, fence, lease, foundation state/result/receipt digests, signer-set digest/count, and committed inclusive deadline.
3. Mismatched cut/operation/artifact/identity/lineage/quorum/deadline input fails closed before any serving-eligibility transition.
4. The committed inclusive deadline survives durable publication/restart and is validated against canonical finalization time; no caller-local clock or arbitrary expiry becomes authority.

6. Focused positive and negative tests cover exact binding, stale/wrong substitutions, insufficient quorum, deadline mismatch, replay/restart, and redaction.
7. #274 remains unbound until this interface is terminal and ancestral, then consumes it without modifying predecessor-owned authority contracts.

## Non-goals

- No #274 Observatory state-machine implementation in this defect.
- No #273 Shepherd behavior change.

Fresh #274 design review at origin/main `bfd811dbb204daae393b073a8dfac3df62e1ba53`, initialized generation 2 digest `293e4209f377d0aa2629d040857fdd5de16b00c7e94112826653f99e08a4592b`, reported two P1 findings: the authenticated cut lacks quorum/lineage/operation/trust-domain/polis bindings, and the accepted inputs lack an authenticated committed expiry/time source. issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC v2][defect] Keep deferred-validator admission consistent across ready transition
issues.body:
## Problem

C-SDLC v2 has a lifecycle protocol contradiction for an initialized issue with explicitly declared future validators. Doctor accepts bounded deferred validator targets only while the record is `initialized`, then recommends `advance_ready`. After that typed transition, the same unchanged reviewed packet is blocked because deferred admission is disabled in `ready`, and the lifecycle has no supported `ready -> initialized` recovery.

Issue #342 is the current read-only reproduction. Its approved initialized packet passed its issue-owned preparation validator and doctor with two exact future issue-owned validators declared through non-placeholder defer reasons. After typed `advance_phase` to `ready`, doctor at generation 12 reports `validator_target_missing` for both unchanged future targets. Creating placeholder product validators would violate the reviewed preparation boundary, while product implementation before bind is prohibited.

This is a regression/gap in the closed #79 contract, which was intended to permit safe direct bind of explicitly deferred targets. It is a tooling defect and must not be absorbed into #342 product scope.

## Source evidence

- `csdlc-v2/src/cards.rs:2452-2493`: `execution_readiness_findings_for_cards` passes `allow_deferred = phase == LifecyclePhase::Initialized`.
- `csdlc-v2/src/cards.rs:2547-2569`: a missing validator target is accepted only when `explicitly_deferred_validator` returns true; otherwise doctor emits `validator_target_missing`, and only an existing or accepted deferred target counts toward the issue-specific denominator.
- `csdlc-v2/src/doctor.rs:245-254`: every finding-free initialized diagnosis reports `next_operation = advance_ready`.
- `csdlc-v2/src/lifecycle.rs:650-670`: bind accepts initialized only when doctor says ready.
- `csdlc-v2/src/lifecycle.rs:808-823`: direct bind already advances `initialized -> ready -> bound` atomically.
- `csdlc-v2/src/model.rs:38-49`: there is no `ready -> initialized` transition.
- `csdlc-v2/tests/gate2.rs:637-755`: the #79 regression proves direct bind from initialized and expects missing targets to fail after bind, but does not exercise the doctor-recommended explicit `advance_ready` step.

## Required outcome

Make doctor guidance, explicit ready transition, deferred-validator admission, and bind behavior one coherent protocol. A reviewed packet that is valid for direct initialized bind must not be stranded by following doctor's advertised next operation. The solution must preserve fail-closed behavior after execution binding and must not reinterpret deferred work as passed proof.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Doctor never recommends an operation that turns its current pass state into an unrecoverable block for an unchanged packet.
2. An initialized issue satisfying the bounded #79 deferred-target predicates has one documented typed path to bind without creating product or validator placeholders before bind.
3. If `advance_ready` remains a supported advertised step, the exact unchanged deferred packet remains bindable in `ready`, or a supported typed lossless recovery returns it to the bindable state.
4. Deferred admission remains restricted to exact issue-owned target and deliverable paths, non-placeholder defer reasons, proving lanes, and fail-closed policy; arbitrary missing/unroutable/non-proving targets still block.
5. After bind, missing declared validators, zero selected tests, or absent proof still fail closed and deferred planning is not treated as execution evidence.
6. A regression test follows the actual advertised sequence: initialized doctor PASS and `advance_ready` recommendation, typed ready transition, ready doctor/bind behavior, bound missing-target failure, then materialized-target PASS.
7. Existing #79 positive and negative deferred-target tests remain green, together with focused C-SDLC v2 tests and strict Clippy.
8. Exact-head independent review confirms lifecycle consistency and no widening of pre-bind implementation authority.

## Non-goals

- No #342 card, lifecycle, product, validator, GitHub, bind, or implementation mutation.
- No placeholder files to satisfy doctor.
- No weakening of post-bind proof requirements.
- No broad lifecycle redesign or manual record rewriting.

## Current safe handling

Until this defect lands, a ready record already affected by the contradiction must use only a separately reviewed typed recovery plan based on real executable preparation denominators; do not create empty future product validators or hand-edit lifecycle state.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Support initialized code-repository declaration for legacy issue authority
issues.body:
## Problem

Legacy issue records for #5837 and #5838 remain initialized/unbound and still use issue authority `danielbaustin/agent-design-language`, while the active code repository and `origin` are `agent-logic/agent-design-language`. Their local records have no explicit `code_repository`, so current doctor blocks with `repository_identity_drift` before design/readiness can pass.

The apparent supported owner operation is `csdlc-issue migrate-code-repository`; it represents code-repository migration, but it rejects initialized records. That leaves prepared, unbound legacy-authority issues unable to declare canonical code-repo authority without binding or hand-editing lifecycle state.

## Exact reproduction

From the current primary checkout:

```sh
.adl/bin/csdlc-v2/csdlc-doctor --issue 5837
.adl/bin/csdlc-v2/csdlc-doctor --issue 5838
.adl/bin/csdlc-v2/csdlc-issue migrate-code-repository --request .git/csdlc-v2/requests/5837-migrate-code-repository-current-20260813.json
.adl/bin/csdlc-v2/csdlc-issue migrate-code-repository --request .git/csdlc-v2/requests/5838-migrate-code-repository-current-20260813.json
```

Observed migration failures:

- #5837 request: `.git/csdlc-v2/requests/5837-migrate-code-repository-current-20260813.json`
- #5837 error: `.git/csdlc-v2/requests/5837-migrate-code-repository-current-20260813.error.json`
- #5838 request: `.git/csdlc-v2/requests/5838-migrate-code-repository-current-20260813.json`
- #5838 error: `.git/csdlc-v2/requests/5838-migrate-code-repository-current-20260813.error.json`

Both fail with status `65`, code `invalid_transition`, message `code repository migration requires bound, implemented, or reviewed phase`.

Current records:

- #5837: initialized, unbound, issue repository `danielbaustin/agent-design-language`, `code_repository` absent/null; after preparation recovery it is gen 42 digest `01b9b2ce7b9f577e02feab7a234243e3838ddaf8cdf194509d2d54745e5950ec`; doctor now blocks on repository drift plus pending design review.
- #5838: initialized, unbound, issue repository `danielbaustin/agent-design-language`, `code_repository` absent/null`; doctor blocks on repository drift.

## Required outcome

Provide one typed owner route that lets initialized, unbound legacy-authority issues declare or recover explicit canonical code-repository authority without binding, branch/worktree mutation, GitHub mutation, publication, merge, closeout, or hand-edited state.

The route may either extend `csdlc-issue migrate-code-repository` to initialized records or add a separate initialized recovery operation, but it must preserve legacy issue authority and append-only lifecycle truth.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A typed request can set or recover `code_repository = agent-logic/agent-design-language` for an initialized issue whose issue repository remains `danielbaustin/agent-design-language`.
2. The route requires exact issue, expected generation, expected digest, actor, reason, source issue repository, and target code repository.
3. The route fails closed on stale generation/digest, ambiguous repository identity, same-number canonical collision ambiguity, non-null branch/worktree mutation, publication/merge/closeout mutation, or missing reason.
4. The route appends auditable lifecycle evidence and increments generation/digest without rewriting prior audit entries, design/diagram bytes, cards outside necessary identity/repository fields, or terminal/publication state.
5. After route plus valid design review, `csdlc-doctor` and `csdlc-validate issue` can pass for initialized/unbound preparation records that are otherwise ready.
6. Bound/implemented/reviewed migration behavior remains backward compatible.
7. Regression fixtures cover #5837/#5838 style initialized legacy issue authority with canonical code repository and no bind.

## Non-goals

- No GitHub issue transfer or bulk repository migration.
- No raw GitHub writes or lifecycle fallback.
- No binding, implementation, PR publication, merge, or terminal closeout.
- No mutation of #5837/#5838 semantics beyond explicit code-repository authority.
- No credential access or provider/runtime proof.

## Why this is needed now

#5837 and #5838 can be safely prepared to ready/unbound only after this repository drift has a typed owner route. Leaving it as an informal blocker causes repeated lifecycle stalls and invites unsafe hand edits.

issues.body:
## Source

issues.title: [v0.92][tools] Add typed bound issue identity/repository migration for split-authority recovery
issues.body:
## Summary

C-SDLC v2 has no typed operation to retarget an already-bound/published issue record when the GitHub issue authority was bootstrapped against the wrong repository/issue identity but the implementation PR is otherwise valid.

This blocks terminal closeout for #5913 / PR #320.

## Reproduction from live #5913

- Legacy issue authority exists: `danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5913` is open.
- Current-repo canonical issue was created through typed owner: `agent-logic/agent-design-language#322`.
- Implementation PR exists and is green: `agent-logic/agent-design-language#320` at head `15bcf79f6c80e18c340db2f3d4de9c43099a5046`.
- Bound worktree: `/Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-5913-adl-review-routing`.
- Current bound record identity:
  - `.csdlc/issues/5913/index.json`
  - `issue = 5913`
  - `repository = agent-logic/agent-design-language`
  - `code_repository = agent-logic/agent-design-language`
  - `phase = published`
  - `generation = 28`
  - `digest = 71793d70dc38f4397e583b52ec1c576a1c7fbe22f1681deb54aebe0061b16715`
  - `publication.repository = agent-logic/agent-design-language`
  - `publication.issue = 5913`
  - `publication.pull_request = 320`
- Live current repo has no issue `#5913`; `gh issue view 5913 --repo agent-logic/agent-design-language` fails to resolve.
- PR #320 has `closingIssuesReferences = []` because `Closes #5913` points at a nonexistent current-repo issue.

## Existing supported routes are insufficient

- `csdlc-issue migrate-code-repository` only sets `code_repository` when absent and only in bound/implemented/reviewed phases. It rejects this case because the record is already published and already has `code_repository`.
- `csdlc-finish` and `csdlc-finish --historical-request` both validate canonical identity and reject mismatched issue/repository authority:
  - `request.issue == record.issue`
  - `request.repository` / `request.issue_repository == record.repository`
  - publication evidence must match the exact finish request.
- Hand-editing `.csdlc/issues/*` would violate lifecycle truth and is not acceptable.

## Required outcome

Add a bounded typed owner operation, tentatively `migrate-bound-issue-identity` or equivalent, that can forward-migrate an existing active bound lifecycle record from one issue identity to another when all safety invariants are proven.

For the live recovery, it must be able to migrate:

- source: `agent-logic/agent-design-language#5913` record namespace
- target: `agent-logic/agent-design-language#322` issue authority
- code/PR authority: `agent-logic/agent-design-language#320`

## Safety invariants

The operation must fail closed unless it proves at least:

1. Source record generation/digest match the request.
2. Source record is active and nonterminal; supported phases should be explicit.
3. Target issue exists in the requested repository and is open.
4. Target issue title/body/provenance matches the intended migration or carries an operation marker proving typed creation.
5. Source and target issue identities are not both active in local `.csdlc/issues/` with conflicting lifecycle truth.
6. Source worktree/branch topology remains exact and clean except generated lifecycle locks.
7. Code repository / publication repository / PR number / base / head / head SHA remain exact.
8. Existing review evidence remains attached to the same substantive code revision and scope, or the operation clears review/publication truth and requires rerun review before publication.
9. Publication evidence is either cleared for republish or forward-updated only through `csdlc-publish` so the PR body uses canonical current issue linkage (`Closes #322`).
10. Append-only audit/provenance records preserve the legacy identity and do not silently erase historical #5913 evidence.

## Non-goals

- Do not add a generic raw JSON/state editor.
- Do not weaken `csdlc-finish` identity checks.
- Do not let finish close or merge against a nonexistent issue authority.
- Do not hand-edit card projections or bypass typed publication.
- Do not mutate #112, #298, or unrelated WP-18C work.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A typed request schema and owner binary command exist for bound issue identity/repository migration or an equivalently named recovery route.
2. Unit/regression tests cover the #5913 -> #322 shape: wrong active issue number, existing current target issue, green already-published PR, and finish invariants that previously blocked closeout.
3. The operation preserves/records source identity provenance and produces a valid target record/cards namespace that passes `csdlc-validate issue`.
4. The operation does not allow arbitrary identity rewrites, terminal record rewrites, or conflicting target namespaces.
5. After migration, `csdlc-publish` can update PR #320 to `Closes #322`, and `csdlc-finish` can resolve both the PR authority and the canonical issue authority without special casing.

## Blocked work

This is blocking terminal closeout for `agent-logic/agent-design-language#320` / canonical issue `#322`. PR #320 should remain unmerged until this operation lands and the lifecycle record is recovered through the typed route.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Prevent publication metadata tail from blocking exact-clean finish
issues.body:
## Problem

Recent publication-tail cases on #295/#301/#298 exposed a C-SDLC v2 recursion: `csdlc-publish` can push the candidate head and then write local publication metadata after the reviewed/committed head, leaving the issue worktree no longer exact-clean for `csdlc-finish`.

The current source shows the risky ordering in `csdlc-v2/src/bin/csdlc-publish.rs`:

- `prepare_publication` derives intent from the reviewed issue record.
- `persist_intent(&cli.root, &intent)` writes `.csdlc/publication/<issue>.intent.json` before push/PR reconciliation completes.
- `push(...)` may then publish the pre-tail `HEAD`.
- `record_publication(...)` records local lifecycle metadata afterward.

Existing tests recognize committed typed publication metadata as non-staling review evidence, but they do not prove the publish/finish handoff remains exact-clean when publication metadata is produced after the pushed head.

## Evidence

- `csdlc-v2/src/bin/csdlc-publish.rs` writes the local intent file through `persist_intent` before the push and before `record_publication`.
- `persist_intent` targets `.csdlc/publication/<issue>.intent.json`.
- `csdlc-v2/src/finish.rs` requires exact remote PR identity and exact expected head SHA; finish can fail when local metadata tail means the worktree is no longer aligned with the published head.
- `csdlc-v2/tests/gate5.rs` has coverage for committed typed publication metadata not staling review, but not for the uncommitted post-push metadata-tail loop.
- Duplicate preflight on 2026-08-12 found no current issue matching publication-tail / intent-json / exact-clean finish recursion.

## Required outcome

Define and implement one safe publication-tail contract so `csdlc-publish` cannot leave a post-push local metadata tail that prevents exact-clean `csdlc-finish`.

## Proposed ownership

Implementation owner paths:

- `csdlc-v2/src/bin/csdlc-publish.rs`
- `csdlc-v2/src/publication.rs` only if the contract requires typed intent/record shape changes
- focused tests under `csdlc-v2/tests/`, preferably the existing publication/finish gate surfaces

Do not edit active issue worktrees as fixtures. Use isolated temp repositories and scripted provider fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `csdlc-publish` either includes required publication metadata in the exact pushed head, or records local metadata in a way that is explicitly classified as safe and cannot block exact-clean finish.
2. The publish operation order is fail-closed: no successful publication result can leave an uncommitted required lifecycle/publication tail that finish must consume but the remote head does not contain.
3. Retry behavior is deterministic for create/update/noop publication actions and does not duplicate or overwrite publication intent/record truth.
4. `csdlc-finish` can verify the exact published head without requiring a second publication cycle solely to absorb publish-created metadata.
5. Tests cover create, update, noop, interrupted-after-push, interrupted-after-intent, and finish-readiness cases.
6. Existing review-staleness behavior for committed typed metadata remains compatible.

## Non-goals

- No implementation in #295, #301, #298, or other active issue worktrees.
- No PR publication or merge as part of this defect creation.
- No broad lifecycle redesign.
- No weakening of exact-head review, exact-clean finish, or GitHub remote identity checks.
- No treating arbitrary untracked files as safe finish metadata.

## Validation plan

- Add focused Rust tests using isolated temp repos/provider fixtures for publication create/update/noop and interruption boundaries.
- Prove the exact-clean finish readiness path after publish.
- Retain existing tests that classify committed typed publication metadata as review-safe.
- Run focused publication/finish gate tests and strict Clippy for the touched crate/test target.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Persist provenance for title-only issue updates
issues.body:
## Problem

`csdlc-github-issue issue_update` requires an operation key, but title-only updates omit `body`. The current owner appends the operation marker only when a body is supplied, and readback verifies only supplied fields. A title-only mutation can therefore return `reconciled=true` while leaving no durable GitHub-side operation attribution; downstream verification has already misclassified this as `MARKER_MISSING`.

## Outcome

Define and implement one truthful title-only mutation contract that preserves the existing issue body while durably binding the operation key and returning unambiguous readback semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A title-only update preserves all pre-existing body bytes and metadata except the explicitly requested title and the minimal durable provenance representation selected by the design.
2. The required operation key is durably attributable on GitHub and immediate readback verifies it.
3. Retries with the same operation key are idempotent; conflicting reuse fails closed.
4. Existing body-bearing issue updates and markers retain compatibility.
5. Results explicitly distinguish title equality, body preservation, and operation provenance; `reconciled=true` cannot mask absent required provenance.
6. Focused positive, retry, conflict, body-preservation, and legacy body-bearing tests pass.

## Owned paths

- `csdlc-v2/src/github.rs`
- focused GitHub issue-owner tests under `csdlc-v2/tests/`
- issue-local C-SDLC records and evidence

## Dependencies and collision boundary

Independent of #291, #295, and #297/#298. Do not edit `csdlc-v2/src/store.rs`, card identity/recovery code, coverage scripts/config/docs, or active projection-recovery files.

## Non-goals

No raw GitHub mutation path, card/lifecycle redesign, issue-title bulk rewrite, publication, merge, closeout, or product behavior change. Stop before merge.
