issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Support typed authored-design refresh after implemented review recovery
issues.body:
## Problem

Issue #294 cannot truthfully remediate an exact-head review finding because the authoritative authored design and diagram changed after implementation, while the installed C-SDLC v2 owner exposes no implemented-phase typed operation that refreshes the SPP/VPP design bindings and invalidates stale design approval.

At issue #294 generation 28 (`6d1ea10a...`), after a supported `recover_review`, a typed `csdlc-edit apply` design-refresh probe failed closed with `invalid_transition: spp mutation is not allowed during implemented`. Source inspection confirms `refresh_prebind_design_bindings` is invoked only for initialized/ready pre-bind contract repair; implemented `replace_plan_steps` does not refresh authored design/diagram digests or invalidate approval. Direct edits to rendered cards/state are prohibited.

## Required Outcome

Add one bounded typed implemented-phase design-envelope refresh/replan operation that:

- requires current typed review-recovery provenance and cleared implementation review/publication/readiness/terminal truth;
- CAS-binds exact generation and digest;
- validates repository-owned authored design and diagram paths;
- recomputes and atomically updates SPP/VPP authored digests;
- unconditionally invalidates the prior design approval and returns design review to pending;
- records append-only old/new authored digests and approval provenance in audit truth;
- requires a subsequent fresh canonical no-context design review through the normal approval route; and
- preserves implemented execution evidence and issue scope without reopening pre-bind topology.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The new typed operation succeeds from implemented only after a current supported review recovery and fails from reviewed/published/terminal or with active assignment/review/publication/readiness truth.
2. Stale generation/digest, unsafe authored paths, missing/drifted artifacts, or mismatched SPP/VPP bindings fail closed without partial mutation.
3. Success atomically refreshes both authored digests, records old/new values, and sets design review pending.
4. Existing execution/history/audit truth remains append-only and implementation phase remains implemented.
5. Fresh design approval is required before a new implementation review assignment/publication.
6. Focused positive, phase/CAS/path/drift/partial-failure, stale-approval, and recovery-provenance tests pass.

## Scope

Typed C-SDLC v2 card/design authority and focused tests only. Do not absorb issue #294 product behavior or issue #291 store work.

## Dependency

Blocked by #297 terminal and ancestral preserved failed-projection recovery integration. Blocks #294 until #296 is terminal and ancestral.

Closes no existing issue.

issues.title: [v0.92][CI][coverage][defect] Classify mechanical compile-fallout without weakening changed-source coverage
issues.body:
## Problem

PR #290 / issue #258 has mechanical compile-fallout in coverage instrumentation that is currently indistinguishable from behavior-bearing changed-source coverage loss. The specific evidence is a tiny import/argument pass-through change in `transport/core.rs`, but there is no supported fail-closed exception path that classifies this kind of compile-only fallout without weakening the changed-source coverage gate.

## Exact evidence

- PR: #290
- Issue: #258
- File: `transport/core.rs`
- Diff scale: `8+ / 1-`
- Mechanical pass-throughs: four `AUTHORITY_BOUND_CERTIFICATE_ACCESS` pass-throughs
- Whole-file coverage observed: `23.51%`
- Retained-file coverage state: `12/13` retained files green
- Current problem: no supported exception for mechanical compile fallout that preserves the 80% changed-source coverage gate.

The required classification must distinguish import-only / argument-pass-through compile fallout to already-governed APIs from semantic behavior changes. It must not create a broad path allowlist or weaken the coverage contract.

## Required scope

Implement fail-closed classification for mechanical compile-fallout coverage cases:

- exact diff parser for import-only or argument-pass-through changes to already governed APIs;
- compile proof for every hunk;
- mapped behavioral proof for every owning API path, including `EstablishedRuntimeAuthority`;
- machine receipt with file, hunk, token, owner, tests, and rationale;
- negative cases for semantic changes, predicate changes, branch changes, state changes, error changes, and unmapped files;
- preserve the 80% changed-source coverage gate;
- keep PR-fast evidence non-authoritative.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: The classifier accepts only exact import-only or argument-pass-through diffs to already governed APIs.
- AC-2: Every accepted hunk has compile proof.
- AC-3: Every owning API path has mapped behavioral proof, including `EstablishedRuntimeAuthority`.
- AC-4: The machine receipt records file, hunk, token, owner, tests, and rationale.
- AC-5: Negative fixtures reject semantic changes, predicate changes, branch changes, state changes, error changes, and unmapped files.
- AC-6: The 80% changed-source coverage gate remains intact and fail-closed.
- AC-7: No blanket path allowlist is introduced.
- AC-8: No nightly/full exclusion is introduced.
- AC-9: PR-fast evidence remains non-authoritative.
- AC-10: #258 republication is blocked until this issue is terminal and ancestral.

## Required tests

- Positive: import-only diff to an already governed API emits a complete machine receipt.
- Positive: argument-pass-through diff for `AUTHORITY_BOUND_CERTIFICATE_ACCESS` emits a complete machine receipt when owning API proof is present.
- Positive: mapped owner proof includes `EstablishedRuntimeAuthority`.
- Negative: semantic body changes are rejected.
- Negative: predicate changes are rejected.
- Negative: branch/control-flow changes are rejected.
- Negative: state mutation changes are rejected.
- Negative: error-path changes are rejected.
- Negative: unmapped files are rejected.
- Gate: 80% changed-source coverage remains enforced for all non-exempt changed source.

## Non-goals

- No blanket path allowlist.
- No weakening of the 80% changed-source coverage gate.
- No nightly/full coverage exclusion.
- No treating PR-fast coverage as authoritative.
- No #258 product behavior change.
- No #203/#205 parent completion.
- No cloud, hosted paid expansion, or optional job expansion.
- No merge, closeout, or republication authority in this issue creation ceremony.

## Dependency

This issue must be terminal and ancestral before #258 republication.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Recover initialized design identity and artifact paths before bind
issues.body:
## Problem

#292 cannot safely bind because its initialized design envelope contains two independent pre-bind defects:

1. Design approval reviewer identity is noncanonical for #119.
2. Authored design/diagram paths were bootstrapped under `.git/csdlc-v2/requests`, which cannot be materialized into a linked Git worktree because `.git` is a file there.

This blocks #292 before implementation. #292 must not resume until this prerequisite is terminal and ancestral.

## Exact #292 reproduction

Repository: `agent-logic/agent-design-language`

Issue #292 initialized state:

- generation: `3`
- digest: `30582acbb4811ca9b50a822a834c45a9302a25fa470f267fd6f4e74a637d1ec8`
- phase: `initialized`
- design path: `.git/csdlc-v2/requests/292-bootstrap-design.md`
- diagram path: `.git/csdlc-v2/requests/292-bootstrap-diagram.mmd`
- intended bind worktree: `/Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-292-implemented-card-identity-repair`
- intended branch: `codex/292-implemented-card-identity-repair`

Recorded noncanonical approval:

```json
"design_review": {
  "approved": {
    "reviewer": "fresh-session:/root/issue_292_fresh_design_review",
    "revision": "8e44dcc8af9c421068df6ab2ab4f8f960680d45e8c9b279e12d2a2a357c40895"
  }
}
```

Actual projectless reviewer evidence:

- reviewer thread/session UUID: `019ff5eb-c6ed-7f83-9d6c-87b7a661eb8b`
- reviewer turn id: `019ff5eb-c752-7b62-aaeb-b374a6e1b040`
- spawned task: `/root/issue_292_fresh_design_review`
- spawn used `fork_turns: "none"`
- subagent metadata: `thread_source: "subagent"`, `agent_path: "/root/issue_292_fresh_design_review"`, nickname `Sartre`
- review result: PASS/no actionable design findings at issue generation `2`, digest `e98def35dd77531ab6c71de59a92fb8ebfd477c1c896bedd12c8f0833e38917a`

The review was genuinely projectless/no-inheritance, but the recorded reviewer string is not canonical `fresh-session:<UUID>`.

Bind failure:

```json
{"code":"unsafe_checkout","message":"authored artifact path contains a symlink or non-directory ancestor","schema":"csdlc.error.v1"}
```

Cause: `csdlc-bind` materializes authored artifacts by preserving relative path. In linked worktrees `.git` is a file, not a directory, so `.git/csdlc-v2/requests/...` cannot be copied as an authored artifact path.

## Required scope

Implement a typed initialized operation to correct the initialized design envelope before bind:

- correct design approval reviewer identity to canonical `fresh-session:<UUID>` only when evidence proves the prior review was projectless/no-inheritance and reviewed the same design digest;
- relocate `design_path` and `diagram_path` atomically from unsafe `.git/...` paths to safe repository-owned non-`.git` paths;
- preserve old and new paths, old and new digests, old and new reviewer identity, reviewed generation/digest, and no-inheritance evidence in append-only audit;
- invalidate stale approval when path/content changes require it;
- require reapproval after relocation or reviewer correction unless the typed route can prove byte-identical artifact content and canonical reviewer evidence at the same reviewed digest;
- keep issue initialized/unbound with branch/worktree null until normal bind;
- reject history loss, manual record edits, and unsafe path ancestors.

Also update bootstrap validation so future issue bootstrap rejects authored design/diagram paths under `.git/...` before the bind-time failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: A typed initialized recovery operation can atomically correct design approval reviewer identity and relocate design/diagram paths before bind.
- AC-2: The operation is generation/digest guarded and append-only.
- AC-3: The operation records old/new reviewer, old/new design path, old/new diagram path, old/new design/diagram digests, reviewed generation/digest, reviewer thread/session UUID, and no-inheritance evidence.
- AC-4: The operation invalidates stale approval and requires reapproval when path/content/reviewer proof is insufficient.
- AC-5: The operation rejects noncanonical reviewer identities unless backed by a concrete projectless session UUID and no-inheritance evidence.
- AC-6: The operation rejects `.git/...`, symlinked, absolute, parent-traversal, issue-control, or otherwise unsafe authored artifact paths.
- AC-7: Bootstrap rejects `.git/...` authored paths directly.
- AC-8: A linked worktree bind fixture reproducing #292 succeeds after recovery and fails before recovery with the current `unsafe_checkout` cause.
- AC-9: Negative tests cover wrong phase, stale generation/digest, missing old artifact, digest drift, unsafe new path, manual-history rewrite attempt, and missing reviewer evidence.
- AC-10: #292 can resume only after this prerequisite is terminal and ancestral.

## Required tests

- Unit: initialized recovery corrects reviewer identity only with canonical UUID evidence.
- Unit: initialized recovery relocates design/diagram paths atomically and preserves byte-identical content.
- Unit: stale generation/digest fails without mutation.
- Unit: unsafe paths including `.git/...`, absolute paths, parent traversal, symlink ancestors, and issue control files fail closed.
- Unit: approval is invalidated when artifact content changes or reviewer proof is incomplete.
- Unit: append-only audit includes old/new reviewer, paths, digests, reviewed generation/digest, and no-inheritance evidence.
- Integration fixture: #292-style initialized record with `.git/...` authored paths fails bind before recovery and binds successfully after recovery into a linked worktree.
- Negative fixture: recovery rejects bound/implemented/reviewed/published/terminal phases unless a separate contract deliberately extends scope.
- Bootstrap fixture: bootstrap rejects `.git/...` design/diagram paths before issue projection creation.

## Non-goals

- No #292 product operation implementation.
- No #112 mutation.
- No manual record edits.
- No generic lifecycle rewrite.
- No bootstrap/bind/implementation in this issue creation ceremony.
- No merge or closeout authority.

## Dependency

#292 is blocked on this prerequisite. This issue must be terminal and ancestral to #292 before #292 resumes.

[v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Repair implemented card identity after issue decomposition
issues.body:
Source contract: `/Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-112-layer8-authority-preparation-v2/.csdlc/evidence/112/IMPLEMENTED_PHASE_CARD_IDENTITY_REPAIR_CONTRACT.md`

## Why this is needed for #112

#112 was decomposed after its authoritative bound branch already existed. The live GitHub issue title/body are now canonical for the retained core:

`[v0.92][WP-18C.02a][112.a] Define shared Layer 8 signed authority core`

However the six local C-SDLC card value envelopes still carry the old pre-decomposition identity:

- title: `[v0.92][WP-18C.02] Govern Layer 8 identity, authority, refusal, and audit`
- slug: `wp18c02-layer8-conversation-authority`

Because #119 review and publication require exact title/body/card/review consistency, #112 cannot truthfully request a new fresh-session review or publication while this mismatch is known.

## Existing route audit

No supported existing operation repairs this implemented-phase identity drift.

- `csdlc-edit schema` exposes `update_identity_version`, but no title/slug identity operation.
- `csdlc-v2/tests/card_identity.rs` covers version-only identity update and does not cover title/slug.
- `csdlc-v2/tests/gate2.rs` asserts normal edits preserve identity title and slug while only advancing generation.
- `csdlc-issue migrate-bound-topology` is not applicable. It migrates old bound-topology records and preserves cards; it is not a post-decomposition semantic identity repair route.
- #291 is initialized-phase only and explicitly says its proposed route should operate only on initialized records unless later extended. This issue must not widen or absorb #291's initialized-phase recovery scope.

## Minimal owner

Recommended owner: `csdlc-edit`.

The editor already owns:

- generation/digest CAS
- per-card value projections
- cross-card identity checks
- rendering and hydration
- audit events
- phase-aware semantic operation authorization

## Minimal operation shape

Add one semantic operation:

```json
{
  "operation": "correct_identity_title_slug_after_decomposition",
  "title": "[v0.92][WP-18C.02a][112.a] Define shared Layer 8 signed authority core",
  "slug": "wp18c02a-112a-shared-layer8-signed-authority-core"
}
```

The operation should be submitted through normal `csdlc-edit apply`:

```json
{
  "issue": 112,
  "card": "sip",
  "expected_generation": 77,
  "expected_digest": "713bfd99665a5e29b267391ebfa11d825d739ffe48d2a73c1ae8e4543ad96d0e",
  "actor": "codex-session-112",
  "reason": "repair implemented-phase card identity after approved #112 decomposition",
  "operation": {
    "operation": "correct_identity_title_slug_after_decomposition",
    "title": "[v0.92][WP-18C.02a][112.a] Define shared Layer 8 signed authority core",
    "slug": "wp18c02a-112a-shared-layer8-signed-authority-core"
  }
}
```

The `card` field should be ignored or constrained to `sip`; the operation must update all six cards atomically so cross-card identity never becomes split.

## Required authorization predicates

The operation should be allowed only when all of the following are true:

1. The issue is in `implemented` phase.
2. `review_assignment`, `review`, `publication`, `readiness`, and `terminal` are all absent.
3. The latest review-related audit operation is `recover_review`.
4. The live issue title/body have been exact-read through typed `csdlc-github-issue issue_read`, or the request carries a retained evidence path and digest for that read.
5. The requested title equals the live canonical issue title from the evidence.
6. The requested title names the retained decomposed issue identity and does not claim #265, #270, #271, #114, #115, #116, #117, Runtime ingress, served acknowledgement/API protocol, Observatory UI, durable history, rooms, roster, or presence ownership.
7. The requested slug is nonempty, normalized, and does not collide with another issue record in the local store.
8. The operation changes only card identity `title`, `slug`, and normal generation/digest/audit projections.

## Audit record

The audit operation should retain old and new values:

```json
{
  "operation": "correct_identity_title_slug_after_decomposition",
  "previous_title": "[v0.92][WP-18C.02] Govern Layer 8 identity, authority, refusal, and audit",
  "new_title": "[v0.92][WP-18C.02a][112.a] Define shared Layer 8 signed authority core",
  "previous_slug": "wp18c02-layer8-conversation-authority",
  "new_slug": "wp18c02a-112a-shared-layer8-signed-authority-core",
  "live_issue_evidence": ".git/csdlc-v2/requests/112-title-gate-issue-read.json"
}
```

## Required tests

1. Implemented-phase card identity correction updates title/slug across all six cards and preserves card content.
2. Correction rejects stale generation/digest.
3. Correction rejects if any review assignment, review result, publication, readiness, or terminal truth is present.
4. Correction rejects outside implemented phase unless a separate phase-specific contract is deliberately added.
5. Correction rejects empty, malformed, or sibling-claiming title/slug.
6. Correction rejects if live issue evidence title does not match the requested title.
7. Correction preserves cross-card identity equality and advances card generation.
8. Correction leaves `csdlc-validate issue --issue 112` passing on the #112 fixture.

## #112 first-consumer sequence

After this operation exists and is separately routed to #112:

1. Apply the typed identity repair to #112.
2. Commit the resulting lifecycle-only repair.
3. Re-run `csdlc-validate issue --issue 112`.
4. Verify all six `.identity.title` and `.identity.slug` values are canonical.
5. Assign a new `fresh-session:<UUID>` reviewer after the repair commit and before any review activity.
6. Record PASS only if the fresh reviewer has no actionable findings.
7. Enforce publication title gate before any PR creation.

## Ownership and non-goals

- #112 is the first consumer and proving fixture, but this tooling issue does not own or implement #112 product behavior.
- Do not mutate #112 cards, branch, worktree, implementation, review, or publication state as part of this issue creation.
- Do not widen, replace, or absorb #291's initialized-phase recovery contract.
- Do not bootstrap, bind, publish, merge, close out, or repair lifecycle state during issue creation.
- Do not claim sibling scope or change any other issue graph.
- Do not bypass `csdlc-edit` with direct Markdown or state-file edits.


## Blocked prerequisite

#292 is blocked before bind or implementation on #294: `[v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Recover initialized design identity and artifact paths before bind`. The prerequisite must be terminal and ancestral before #292 resumes because current #292 pre-bind staging has a noncanonical design approval reviewer (`fresh-session:/root/issue_292_fresh_design_review` instead of canonical `fresh-session:019ff5eb-c6ed-7f83-9d6c-87b7a661eb8b`) and unsafe authored design/diagram paths under `.git/csdlc-v2/requests` that make `csdlc-bind` fail with `unsafe_checkout`.

No #292 product operation, #112 fixture mutation, bootstrap, bind, implementation, publication, merge, or manual record edit is authorized until #294 lands and #292 is recovered through typed tooling.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Recover initialized decomposed issue cards without rewriting history
issues.body:
Source candidate: `/Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-114-durable-history-preparation/.adl/session-handoffs/ISSUE_114_INITIALIZED_PHASE_RECOVERY_GAP_CANDIDATE.md`

## Problem statement

An initialized C-SDLC v2 issue can become stale after live issue-graph decomposition. The #114 preparation packet is the concrete reproduction: live #114 was decomposed into #276 -> #277 -> #278 -> parent exact-revision integration, while the local gen0 packet still originated as a monolithic durable-history implementation issue.

Current typed routes can repair some initialized-phase card fields, but they do not provide one safe, audited recovery contract that can replace every stale semantic surface needed for fresh #119 design/card approval:

- STP acceptance criteria
- SPP plan steps
- SRP scope/prompts
- SOR preparation truth
- identity title/slug
- design-reference semantics, where the preserved design is historical evidence rather than current implementation authority

In #114, later issue-local typed recovery requests did repair STP acceptance criteria, SPP plan steps, SIP operator constraints, SPP risks, and SRP review prompts. The remaining unrepaired gen35 residuals still prevent truthful fresh #119 approval:

- SRP `review_scope` still says: `Exact #114 changed paths, merged #111/#112 contract boundaries, storage/migration/recovery invariants, all PVF evidence, public projections, and no #83 or sibling mutation.`
- SOR still says `summary: "Pre-execution output record."` with empty artifacts/validation/follow-ups.
- card identity still uses title `[v0.92][WP-18C.04] Add durable conversation history, continuity, and receipts` and slug `v0-92-wp-18c-04-durable-conversation-history`.

Because design review must follow #119 procedure and cannot be backfilled, #114 cannot truthfully record fresh design approval while these residuals remain unresolved or undispositioned.

## Concrete #114 reproduction state

Use this existing local packet without modifying #114:

- Worktree: `/Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-114-durable-history-preparation`
- Branch: `codex/114-wp18c04-durable-history-preparation`
- Issue record: `.csdlc/issues/114/index.json`
- Generation: `35`
- Digest: `3ceb6fa642b537692a097960e4c216f354de777ece387cc82c3b8022e27b2e51`
- Phase: `initialized`
- Design review: `pending`
- Issue record branch/worktree: `null` / `null`
- Audit entries: `36`

Preserved historical evidence:

- `.csdlc/prepared/issues/114/design.md`
  - byte sha256: `1017526669c138e76ed815304afaddd316665149ce9739b2b143f6827936a2c8`
  - C-SDLC authored digest: `b70cf7e77e06cad287166597bf0b70bfcd43392f6452325c905dcec6fab65c08`
- `.csdlc/prepared/issues/114/diagram.mmd`
  - byte sha256: `06818f0c057e01a83e9c54c7f7a7812b20565ce9a371883b17bf46d48d69760f`
  - C-SDLC authored digest: `b8e5984d673cff4cb398de9deeb653bfb7dda81c388243371d91bd7562bebf42`

Validation at gen35:

- `python3 .csdlc/prepared/issues/114/validate_preparation_bundle.py` passes and reports generation `35`.
- `csdlc-doctor --repo /Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-114-durable-history-preparation --issue 114` blocks only on `design_review_missing_or_stale`.
- `csdlc-validate --root /Volumes/FastWork/adl-worktrees/adl-issue-114-durable-history-preparation issue --issue 114` fails closed because it wraps the same doctor blocker.

## Exact rejected or unavailable operation evidence

- SIP `replace_operator_constraints` during `initialized`: rejected as `invalid_transition`; later repaired at audit sequence 34 via `correct_operator_constraints_before_bind`.
- STP `replace_acceptance_criteria` during `initialized`: rejected as `invalid_transition`; later repaired at audit sequence 32 by a typed recovery request.
- SPP `replace_plan_steps` during `initialized`: rejected as `invalid_transition`; later repaired at audit sequence 33 by a typed recovery request.
- SRP `set_field review_scope` during `initialized`: rejected as `srp mutation is not allowed during initialized`; no later safe repair route found.
- SOR semantic updates during `initialized`/`pre_phase`: no supported preparation-summary repair route found.
- identity title/slug replacement during initialized recovery: no supported operation found in `csdlc-edit schema`.

Supporting packet evidence:

- `.adl/session-handoffs/issue_114_recovery_acceptance_request.json`
- `.adl/session-handoffs/issue_114_recovery_plan_steps_request.json`
- `.adl/session-handoffs/issue_114_recovery_operator_constraints_request.json`
- `.adl/session-handoffs/issue_114_recovery_risks_request.json`
- `.adl/session-handoffs/issue_114_recovery_srp_prompts_request.json`
- `.csdlc/issues/114/audit.jsonl` sequences 32 through 36

## Proposed owner binary and contract

Recommended owner: `csdlc-edit`.

Recommended contract: add a typed recovery request/result for initialized post-decomposition semantic regeneration, for example:

- command: `csdlc-edit recover-initialized-decomposition --request <request.json>`
- request schema: `csdlc.initialized_decomposition_recovery.request.v1`
- result schema: `csdlc.initialized_decomposition_recovery.result.v1`

The gap is semantic card regeneration under generation/digest guards. `csdlc-edit` already owns card values, rendering, projection hydration, audit entries, and design approval adjacency. `csdlc-issue` may help compute issue graph inputs, but should not be the primary card rewrite owner. Bootstrap regeneration must not be the primary path because it risks overwriting or reclassifying existing gen0 history instead of explicitly preserving it.

## Safe recovery semantics

The new route should:

- operate only on `initialized` issue records unless explicitly extended later
- require exact `issue`, `expected_generation`, and `expected_digest`
- require explicit `actor`, `reason`, and `recovery_scope`
- require old design/diagram paths plus expected byte and C-SDLC authored digests
- preserve existing design/diagram files byte-for-byte
- record whether the old design is current authority or historical/reference evidence
- replace selected semantic fields atomically:
  - SIP identity title/slug if needed
  - SIP operator constraints
  - STP acceptance criteria
  - SPP plan steps
  - SPP risks/replan triggers/affected areas if needed
  - VPP preparation lanes if needed
  - SRP review scope/prompts/result as preparation review truth
  - SOR preparation summary/artifacts/follow-ups without claiming execution
- refuse if the replacement introduces bind, product implementation, publication, merge, closeout, GitHub mutation, child bootstrap, or #112 worktree mutation
- refuse if the child graph is missing or inverted
- emit one append-only audit entry with changed fields, old/new digests, preserved evidence digests, and non-goal guardrails

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: A typed initialized recovery request can transform a stale decomposed-parent packet to coordination-only truth without binding, branch mutation, GitHub writes, publication, merge, closeout, or product-code changes.
- AC-2: Recovery preserves append-only audit history, issue generation/digest CAS, issue record branch/worktree null state, and every existing design/diagram byte.
- AC-3: Recovery can replace STP acceptance criteria and SPP plan steps or reuse the demonstrated safe repair path while keeping AC/step IDs coherent.
- AC-4: Recovery can replace SRP review scope and prompts so a future #119 review can evaluate the exact preparation packet without inherited implementation-review language.
- AC-5: Recovery can record SOR preparation truth without claiming execution, implementation, publication, merge, or closeout.
- AC-6: Recovery can update identity title/slug to coordination-parent semantics or explicitly mark old identity as retained historical label with Planning disposition.

issues.title: [v0.92][runtime-v3][20.c] Run six-hour Agent Logic Spot qualification only after operator and cost authorization
issues.body:
Split from #20. Part of #20. Depends on terminal #266, #267, terminal/canonical/ancestral #414, and terminal/canonical/ancestral #415.

## Outcome

Under explicit authorization, execute exactly one Spot qualification attempt in the approved Agent Logic business AWS account on exact `r7i.2xlarge` capacity (8 vCPU/64 GiB), retain exact-head evidence, prove controlled cancellation/failure cleanup, and independently prove zero task-owned instances.

## Fixed authorization envelope

- Exactly one Spot attempt; no silent retry or replacement attempt.
- Total wall-clock ceiling 25,200 seconds and total cost ceiling USD 20.
- Exact `r7i.2xlarge`; no On-Demand fallback, GPU, or #269 execution.
- Agent Logic business account/profile verification, deadline, kill switch, exact-owner cleanup, and independent zero-owned-instance readback are mandatory.

## Habitable Runtime denominator

- Consume terminal/canonical/ancestral #414; do not invent another recovery system.
- Exercise multiple distinct resident CPU-local Shepherd agents backed by pinned local models/configurations, including Ollama `llama3.1:8b` Q4, with one active worker at a time, conservative contexts, and no concurrent compilation.
- Every resident performs useful bounded work before interruption.
- Confirmed Spot reclamation closes admission and dehydrates the complete population through existing Runtime v2 quiescent/suspended/dormant and snapshot authority to a retained Runtime volume distinct from build cache.
- Replacement capacity restores every exact identity, state, sequence, predecessor, model/configuration digest before admission with no duplicate or missing activation.
- Every restored resident performs deterministic next useful work.
- Operator status/control plus cold/warm latency, peak RSS, memory headroom, task-result digests, and complete-population recovery fit 8 vCPU/64 GiB with headroom.
- Tamper, partial, rollback, substitution, deadline, duplicate, and missing-agent cases fail closed.
- An optional bounded large external-model call is non-authoritative and never required for admission, continuity, useful local work, or pass/fail.

## Other acceptance

1. Exact approved revision, binaries, configuration, account/profile, region/AZ, Spot identity, AMI, tags, and six-hour workload/fault/recovery denominator are retained.
2. Evidence is exact-head, redacted, complete, and digest-bound without restart erasure.
3. Success, failure, and cancellation terminate only task-owned resources and prove zero remaining task-owned instances.
4. Fresh exact-head review has no unresolved actionable findings.

## First attempt disposition

The first authorized attempt on 2026-08-18 failed during remote immutable-builder `verify_builder_toolchain` with exit 127 before production exposure. Cleanup and zero-owned-instance readback passed, but the remote-only diagnostic was not retained; #415 owns that evidence repair. It did not prove qualification or resident recovery.

## Non-goals

No second attempt, 24-hour qualification, default release promotion, cloud-Polis deployment, personal AWS account, On-Demand fallback, GPU, model-weight serialization, or #269 execution.

## Graph

`#266 + #267 + #414 + #415 -> #268 -> optional #269`; `split_from: #20`; `part_of: #20`.

issues.title: [v0.92][CI] Stop hosted coverage aggregate from recompiling Rust
issues.body:
## Problem

The required hosted coverage path for PRs that need full workspace coverage currently compiles the instrumented workspace repeatedly without adding proportional confidence. The two `adl-coverage-workspace-hosted` matrix shards each compile the same instrumented workspace before collecting partitioned `.profraw` files, and the downstream `adl-coverage-hosted` aggregate job then enters `ADL_AUTHORITATIVE_COVERAGE_REPORT_MODE=report`, calls `compile_instrumented_profile`, and compiles the instrumented workspace again before importing the shard profiles.

For a runtime-heavy PR such as #250, this turns the final required gate into roughly an hour of hosted CI wall time, most of it spent recompiling instead of proving new behavior. This blocks runtime sprint throughput and wastes expensive hosted runner capacity.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` defines `adl-coverage-workspace-hosted (${{ matrix.shard }}/2)` with two independent hosted runners.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` later runs `Aggregate workspace coverage shard profiles` with `ADL_AUTHORITATIVE_COVERAGE_REPORT_MODE=report`.
- `adl/tools/run_authoritative_coverage_lane.sh` report mode calls `compile_instrumented_profile` before importing shard `.profraw` files and generating the summary.

## Scope

Permanently remove redundant hosted workspace coverage recompilation for PR full-coverage runs while preserving fail-closed coverage truth, exact provenance, shard/profile integrity where retained, and the required `adl-coverage-hosted` merge gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- A PR full-coverage hosted path compiles the instrumented workspace at most once for the workspace coverage result that feeds the required aggregate gate.
- The required `adl-coverage-hosted` gate still verifies runtime/workspace provenance and enforces coverage policy truth.
- Coverage summaries remain generated from exact current-head profiles; stale or missing profiles fail closed.
- The fix does not launch optional, paid, cloud, native, soak, or slow proof jobs.
- Focused workflow/script contract tests cover the new command shape and reject reintroducing aggregate report-mode recompilation.

## Non-goals

No runtime product behavior changes, no #199 governed-membership changes, no optional CI expansion, no release coverage ratchet redesign, and no migration to a paid external coverage backend.

issues.title: [backlog][runtime-v3] Support TLS 1.2 on public Axum HTTPS/WSS for Unity
issues.body:
## Problem

Runtime v3's public Axum HTTPS/WSS listener is hard-coded to TLS 1.3 only. Unity 6000.5.1f1's UnityTLS client negotiates TLS 1.2 with otherwise compatible public endpoints and cannot complete the Runtime handshake. This blocks issue #84 even with a valid CA-issued certificate and complete Let’s Encrypt chain.

The restriction is currently explicit in `adl-runtime-kernel/src/tls.rs` through `with_protocol_versions(&[&rustls::version::TLS13])`.

## Diagnostic evidence

The #84 native Unity Play Mode lane established the following controls:

- Unity accepted Let’s Encrypt's official X2-terminating Gen-Y test endpoint.
- Unity rejected direct Root YE trust, as expected.
- A separately issued short-lived ECDSA Wuji leaf with the same YE/X2 certificate shape still failed against the ADL Runtime with UnityTLS error code 7.
- The exact Wuji short-lived leaf and chain succeeded when served by OpenSSL on the same host and port. Unity negotiated TLS 1.2 and advanced past certificate validation to the expected application-layer timeout.
- Therefore the certificate, hostname, ECDSA key, and X2 chain are not the blocker; the Runtime's TLS 1.3-only public listener is the discriminating boundary.

Retained local evidence in the #84 worktree includes:

- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T063900Z-live.log` — official X2 endpoint accepted at TLS layer.
- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T064625Z-live.log` — short-lived Wuji certificate rejected against Runtime.
- `.adl/evidence/84/unity-runtime-v3/20260812T064949Z-live.log` — identical Wuji certificate presentation accepted through OpenSSL; application layer intentionally non-Runtime.

## Required outcome

Support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 on Runtime v3's public Axum HTTPS/WSS listener using the shared reviewed Rustls provider and secure ECDHE cipher suites, while preserving TLS 1.3-only behavior for Quinn Guardian transport where that is a protocol invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- Public Axum HTTPS/WSS server configuration enables both Rustls TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
- TLS 1.2 support is limited to reviewed forward-secret AEAD suites compatible with the configured ECDSA and RSA certificate policies; no legacy TLS versions or weak suites are enabled.
- Quinn Guardian mTLS remains TLS 1.3-only unless a separate reviewed requirement changes it.
- Focused tests prove the public listener accepts TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 and rejects TLS 1.1 and earlier.
- Focused tests cover CA-issued ECDSA identity loading and complete-chain presentation without leaf-as-root trust.
- The real Unity 6000.5.1f1 Play Mode product adapter completes HTTPS and WSS authentication against the Runtime without a proxy, trust-store mutation, custom always-accept certificate handler, or verification bypass.
- Existing browser/curl clients continue to negotiate TLS 1.3 when supported.
- Runtime startup remains fail-closed for invalid identity, incomplete chain, wrong SAN, expiry, unsuitable EKU, and unknown issuer.
- Observability records negotiated TLS version without logging credentials or certificate private material.

## Non-goals

- Disabling certificate validation or adding a Unity-specific trust bypass.
- Installing or mutating host keychain trust.
- Adding a TLS-termination proxy as the product solution.
- Weakening Quinn Guardian mutual authentication.
- Reissuing certificates as a substitute for protocol compatibility.
- Implementing this change inside issue #84.

## Issue graph

- Follow-up to closed TLS standardization issue #92.
- Blocks the real native Unity acceptance lane and publication of #84.
- #84 owns only the Unity consumer and must treat this Runtime change as an upstream dependency.

## Required outcome

- Add an explicit typed correction for `SPP.plan_summary` only on a clean `implemented` record reached by typed review recovery, with review, publication, and readiness truth cleared.
- Permit SIP operator-constraint correction during initialized/ready pre-bind contract repair, preserving CAS, renderer/schema validation, audit history, authored-artifact identity, design invalidation/reapproval requirements, and branch/worktree non-authority before bind.
- Keep ordinary implemented replanning and post-publication mutation fail closed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Issue #5854 can replace its stale five-child SPP summary with the four-child denominator after typed publication/review recovery.
2. Issue #5840 can remove obsolete preparation-claim guidance while remaining initialized and unbound.

issues.body:
Follow-up to #209 and merged PR #215. Blocks #142 until the retained WP-14 native proof is present and machine-validatable on merged `main`.

## Problem

PR #215 passed Linux and macOS native proof at source revision `c640066f284a915b638add377cc4b0a2e221e6f9`, but the later commit retaining the ten-file packet was not part of the merge. Merged `main` therefore has no retained packet, manifest, or validation log, and the canonical validator fails before it can authenticate the proof. The current validator also requires each receipt source SHA to equal the current checkout HEAD, so it cannot validate retained evidence after squash/rebase even when protected production bytes are unchanged.

## Required outcome

- Restore the exact ten retained native packet, manifest, and validation-log artifacts produced for #209 run `31453636709` onto `main`.
- Add a final-head retained-proof validator that verifies all packet digests, runner/job provenance, source manifests, semantic equivalence, and path hygiene.
- Bind the retained source to the final checkout using source ancestry OR protected-tree digest equivalence, while always rejecting protected-source drift.
- Make the proof machine-validatable after ordinary merge, squash, or rebase publication.
- Update the issue-local VPP/SOR proof command through typed lifecycle routes.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The exact eight platform files plus `native-validation-manifest.json` and `native-receipts-validation.log` from #209 run `31453636709` are retained with verified digests and provenance.
2. The existing exact-source validator still authenticates the source-run packet at `c640066f284a915b638add377cc4b0a2e221e6f9`.
3. A retained-proof validator passes at a later final head only when source ancestry or protected-tree digest equivalence is established and every protected path still matches the proved packet.
4. Focused regressions reject missing files, digest tampering, provenance mismatch, semantic mismatch, protected-source drift, and an unrelated/non-equivalent source revision; squash-equivalent history passes.
5. The canonical final-head VPP/SOR validation command invokes the retained-proof validator and passes on the published PR head.
6. Fresh independent design and exact-head implementation reviews have no unresolved actionable findings before publication/merge.
7. The qualified closing PR links #209/PR #215 and #142, and all required checks are green.

## Scope

Only #209 retained evidence, its issue-local native validators/tests, typed lifecycle proof truth, and the smallest workflow/contract adjustment required for merge-safe validation.

## Non-goals

Production runtime behavior changes, replay/ACIP redesign, rerunning unrelated Sprint 4 work, AWS use, cloud provisioning, or merging without operator review.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC v2][blocker] Support truthful initialized-phase acceptance and plan-step repair
issues.body:
## Problem

A preparation package can receive an actionable design-review finding after typed bootstrap but before dependency-authorized binding. At `initialized` or `ready`, `csdlc-edit apply` permits `replace_planning_collection`, but rejects `replace_acceptance_criteria` and `replace_plan_steps` with `<card> mutation is not allowed during initialized`. `csdlc-edit bootstrap` is idempotent-only and rejects changed initialization truth once the issue exists. The only currently accepted phase for those semantic operations is `bound`, which would falsely bind dependency-gated preparation merely to repair design truth.

This blocks issue #205 from truthfully adding an exact protected all-47 manifest contract to STP AC-8 and SPP S3 after review. Hand-editing values/rendered cards is prohibited, and binding #205 before its dependencies merge is prohibited.

## Required outcome

Add a typed, audit-preserving initialized/ready-phase route that can replace STP acceptance criteria and SPP plan steps for an unbound preparation package, atomically regenerate all six projections, refresh design/diagram digests, invalidate stale design approval, and preserve issue identity and prior audit truth.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An existing unbound `initialized` or `ready` issue can apply `replace_acceptance_criteria` and `replace_plan_steps` through a declared typed operation without deleting/rebootstrapping its record.
2. The route preserves repository, issue, initialization lineage, audit history, and all untouched semantic fields.
3. The route atomically regenerates values/rendered/AST projections and refreshes design and diagram digests.
4. Any prior design approval becomes stale or pending and must be independently reapproved at the repaired exact head.
5. Stale generation/digest, malformed AC identifiers, missing acceptance coverage, invalid step status, path/identity drift, bound/implemented misuse, and partial write fail closed.
6. Existing bound-phase execution replan behavior remains unchanged.
7. Focused tests cover the exact #205-style sequence: bootstrap, one initialized planning-collection edit, later AC and plan-step repair, design change, regeneration, doctor, and reapproval readiness.
8. Strict Clippy, focused owner tests, diff hygiene, and independent exact-head review pass before a ready unmerged PR opens.

## Owned scope

- `csdlc-v2/src/cards.rs`
- `csdlc-v2/src/store.rs`
- Focused C-SDLC v2 gate tests
- Issue-local lifecycle/evidence records

## Non-goals

- No weakening of phase, branch, worktree, dependency, review, publication, or merge gates.
- No permission to execute product work while unbound.
- No manual rendered-card or values-file mutation.
- No record deletion or audit reset as a repair mechanism.
- No changes to #205 product scope or proof denominators.

## Publication boundary

The implementation PR must begin with `Closes #<issue>` and stop before merge.

issues.title: [v0.92][WP-04.16b2] Govern learner, joint, and final voter membership transitions
issues.body:
Split from superseded #192 and #142 after independent design review. Depends on #191, core authority protocol #201, and authorized learner/exclusion transport #202.

## Outcome
Make OpenRaft learner, joint, final, removal, and governed rejoin transitions agree exactly with Runtime MembershipState, AuthorityMembership, verified routes, and one crash-reconciled published view, so no learner, removed voter, stale voter, leader, caller, or local history can self-promote or retain authority.

- separate governed EnrollNonVoting, PromoteVoter, and RemoveVoter operations
- authenticated #202 learner admission and exact committed-prefix or canonical-snapshot catch-up

- stable collision-checked guardian-to-Raft-id mapping
- shared pending exclusion and retain=false removal
- reconcile-before-visible MembershipState, AuthorityMembership, and route parity publication
- two-operation stale-state rejoin and crash/restart reconciliation
- focused real secure-node tests and merge-safe proof

## Acceptance

- Existing Raft ids never change, and a candidate id comes only from the digest-bound #201 operation payload.
- Joint and final configurations are durably observable even when OpenRaft applies both in one batch; a committed-joint restart resumes only the exact authorized target.
- Pending removal uses the shared #202 exclusion authority, removes with retain=false, denies ordinary voter/endorsement/renewal/mutation/Shepherd/Observatory authority, and emits only a pending-exclusion receipt for #200.
- No public membership/route/authority view changes until private reconciliation, external checkpoint, result cache, and one atomic published-view generation agree.
- Crashes and exact retries at every phase reconcile deterministically; conflicting or regressed state fails closed.
- Focused tests, strict Clippy, exact receipt, and independent review pass before publication.

Creating #201 tokens, implementing #202 transport, concrete authority-store reconciliation (#200), kernel continuity, Guardian/API/WSS integration, models, AWS, live demonstrations, final #142 delivery, merge without operator authorization, or lifecycle closeout.

Output filtering includes a versioned supported-`jq` subset manifest with explicit unsupported syntax and diagnostics. The contract also pins the exact candidate `cargo-deny` release used from the construction spike onward. V3-02 may recommend changing that candidate only through the same reviewed stop/go architecture-revision path used for any failed spike threshold; it cannot silently substitute a release. V3-01 also freezes a candidate dependency manifest naming every previously open YAML, JSON Schema, middleware, template, and file-locking crate with exact version/features and a pre-spike direct-dependency count. ## Dependencies

## Architecture Decisions

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every public command and output mode has a versioned contract.
2. Every retained v2 invariant maps to one owner issue and proof lane.
3. Exact review, GitHub truth, topology ownership, atomic state, and cleanup boundaries cannot be weakened by later implementation choices.
4. Unknown or intentionally changed v2 behavior is explicit and reviewed.
5. The importer remains available until the later of all v2-origin issues reaching terminal state or the operator-approved rollback window expiring.
6. Output filtering and templating have one approved in-process implementation boundary and cannot invoke a shell or external formatter.
7. Reviewer independence is structurally checked where identity is bindable; policy-only identity cannot silently satisfy publication.
8. Closing and non-closing publication are disjoint typed modes; `PartOf` cannot close or terminally complete its parent issue, and split-repository linkage is qualified in both modes.
9. Every mutable authoritative field has exactly one matrix owner and at least one typed authoring path; every supported invalidation/recovery state has a valid typed next operation. 12. V3-01 approval is blocked until the state-size artifact identifies the actual largest v2 bundle at `f1c01499`, records every measured blob and total, and passes the locked recomputation case; no unmeasured adequacy claim is allowed.
13. If that measurement makes the 10x block impractical for atomic state or operator latency, V3-01 stops and returns to architecture review for a versioned retention/compaction decision; it may neither lower the factor nor proceed with an unbounded aggregate.
14. The same gate proves the complete V3-16 review/recover/card-family canary fits below 50 percent of the block using maximum schema-valid event sizes, so embedded audit growth is represented rather than inferred from typical v2 history.

issues.title: [v0.92][runtime] Operationalize distributed Runtime and polis Observatory across Wuji and AWS
issues.body:
## Goal

Operationalize the merged distributed Runtime as a real three-voter polis through production Guardian and kernel entrypoints and expose exactly one quorum-leased polis Observatory. Run two live demonstrations strictly serially: first three voters on Wuji, then one Wuji voter plus two independently stateful AWS voters in distinct Availability Zones.

## Configuration and shepherd

The canonical Runtime init configuration must include an explicit `shepherd_agent_ref` and governed per-node provider/model profiles. The shepherd launches with the polis, has a distinct non-exportable governed identity, is never a consensus voter, and cannot mint membership, lease, snapshot, fence, activation, mutation, or Observatory authority. Premature AWS shepherd activation and Observatory binding must fail closed.

Wuji may use three smaller local models so all voters fit concurrently. Model capability must never alter authority semantics. Every Wuji and AWS voter uses a pinned, bounded, private self-hosted model through the supported `ollama_http` contract or a separately reviewed compatible local provider. AWS must prove private endpoints, exact artifact identity, restart, bounded cold start, inference under load, hard CPU/memory isolation from consensus, no hosted-model fallback, and complete model-cache teardown.

## Phase A: Wuji only

- Launch exactly three real authenticated Guardian/kernel voters on Wuji.
- Launch the configured non-voting shepherd with the polis.
- Show exactly one live coherent redacted polis Observatory containing all three voters.
- Prove authenticated traffic, a governed mutation, one-voter loss with retained quorum, recovery or truthful fail-closed behavior, and bounded shutdown.
- Produce a complete cleanup receipt for every process, Observatory, port, lock, lease, credential, model, and test root.

Phase B must not start until Phase A cleanup is proven. The two phases must never overlap.

## Phase B: Wuji and AWS continuity

- Verify `agent-logic-admin` resolves to the approved Agent Logic business account.
- Launch one Wuji voter and two AWS voters in distinct Availability Zones with independent state, volumes, interfaces, roles, and private local-model services.
- Govern-admit the distinct AWS shepherd identity while all three voters are healthy.
- Have Wuji propose a snapshot boundary that quorum commits; require both AWS committed indices to match and all healthy voters to independently materialize the same canonical snapshot digest through the native snapshot/catalog path. Manual copying and uncommitted local history are non-proving.
- Serially compact and restart each AWS voter from its snapshot while the other two preserve quorum.
- Saturate bounded local inference while proving consensus timing and starvation safety.
- Keep Wuji alive but asymmetrically partition it without any harness bridge. Require both AWS votes to elect a newer AWS leader before the safety window, Wuji fence, owner activation, and continued governed mutation.
- Wait for the old quorum-enforced Wuji Observatory lease TTL to expire, then activate the AWS shepherd and acquire exactly one replacement Observatory lease. Show the single running Observatory on AWS.
- Heal the partition without restarting Wuji; prove stale Wuji cannot mutate, renew, own the Observatory, or serve stale reads, then demotes and synchronizes only through governed rejoin/recovery.
- Re-partition Wuji and stop the opposite-AZ AWS voter; the remaining one-of-three AWS voter must halt mutation while the colocated shepherd remains alive and reports loss of quorum.
- Tear down every ephemeral compute, volume, network attachment, SSM session, credential, process, model cache, Observatory, port, lock, and test root.

## Production integration remediation

This issue restores the original live #5878 contract that PR #140 narrowed. Completion requires real production Guardian/kernel launch, authenticated API and WSS continuity, live partition, quorum fencing, migration, recovery, continued mutation, Observatory movement, and bounded shutdown. Library registration or in-process module tests alone do not satisfy the issue.

The retained proof contract must also validate truthfully after squash merge onto `main` and reject any protected production, test, config, runner, API, or proof-contract change after the proving revision unless a new exact receipt and review are produced.

## Review and merge

The implementation receives a fresh independent exact-head review. The PR remains unmerged until both serial live demonstrations have been shown to the operator and every required check is green. Lifecycle closeout reconciliation is asynchronous and intentionally outside this implementation issue.

Plan review: Gemini `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, final verdict APPROVE, review id `2RN6atenNYbgz7IPmomJ4As`.

issues.title: [v0.92][tools] Prevent connector and raw-gh fallback for C-SDLC GitHub writes
issues.body:
## Incident

A Codex session attempted to create an ADL issue through the ChatGPT GitHub connector. The connector returned `403 Resource not accessible by integration`. The session then used raw `gh` with the approved token file. The mutation succeeded, proving the shared token remains valid, but both routes violated the existing C-SDLC v2 ownership contract.

This is not a regression in legacy token work #3963, #4087, #4454, or #5655. It is a route-selection and guardrail regression: the repository's root operating instructions did not stop the session before it selected a forbidden write path.

## Required outcome

Make the repo-native Rust GitHub owner path unmistakable and mechanically guarded for every covered ADL issue/PR mutation. Unsupported connector writes must never be attempted, and connector failure must never authorize raw `gh` fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root `AGENTS.md` explicitly prohibits the ChatGPT GitHub connector and raw `gh` for covered lifecycle writes.
- [ ] Root guidance names `csdlc-github-issue`, `csdlc-github-pr`, `csdlc-publish`, and `csdlc-finish` as the only current owners for their respective surfaces.
- [ ] Missing or unavailable installed owner binaries fail closed; they do not authorize fallback.
- [ ] Add a focused repository guard or fitness test that detects drift between root policy and `docs/tooling/ADL_CSDLC_GITHUB_CLIENT_BOUNDARY.md`.
- [ ] Add an incident regression fixture proving a connector 403 cannot be reclassified as a token failure or fallback authorization.
- [ ] Verify issue creation through `csdlc-github-issue` using the approved default token resolver without printing or persisting token contents.
- [ ] Preserve existing shared token precedence and redaction behavior.

## Historical evidence

- Legacy #3963 fixed shared token discovery/redaction.
- Legacy #4087 fixed configured-token propagation.
- Legacy #4454 restored operator-default token discovery.
- Legacy #5655 added the repo-native Rust GitHub mutation surface with no connector dependency.
- The same connector 403 was observed in legacy #5384 and PR #5682.

## Non-goals

- Do not reopen or rewrite the completed token resolver implementations.
- Do not authorize connector writes.
- Do not add raw `gh` fallback.
- Do not expose token contents.
- Do not touch publication recovery issue #100 beyond linking this incident.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC v2][blocker] Reconcile umbrella receipts with v3 source-evidence topology
issues.body:
## Problem

`.csdlc/prepared/issues/5862/validate-implementation-wave.rb` hard-requires each child v2 proof `source_revision` to equal the final child PR head. Current C-SDLC v3 proof truth intentionally uses three revisions: substantive source `S`, a single evidence-introduction commit `E`, and later lifecycle/publication/PR head `H`, where `S != E != H`. The umbrella validator therefore rejects truthful current child receipts or pressures callers toward impossible self-referential evidence.

## Required outcome

Reconcile the Sprint #5862 umbrella receipt validator with the v3 `S -> E -> H` topology without weakening terminal, ancestry, path, evidence, or integration checks.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A valid terminal child/umbrella fixture with `S != E != H` passes.
2. Every exact protected product path is unchanged across `S..E..H`.
3. Evidence is introduced exactly once at `E` and remains byte-immutable through `H`.
4. The exact PR head is `H`; merge revision, ancestry, issue/PR terminal envelope, and candidate mapping remain verified.
5. The validator rejects product drift after `S`, evidence drift after `E`, wrong PR head, wrong merge revision, broken ancestry, ambiguous or missing child mapping, and self-referential/fake evidence.
6. The sixteen-child denominator, exact owned-path denominator, dependency DAG, and terminality requirements are unchanged.
7. #5878 integrated proof and native macOS/Linux/Windows receipt bindings remain mandatory.
8. Focused regression fixtures cover representative current v3 child topologies as well as every rejection above.
9. Existing valid v2/same-revision topology remains supported only where it satisfies the same immutable product/evidence and terminality checks.
10. Focused tests, applicable strict lint/syntax checks, exact-head independent review, and green CI pass.

## Validation

Run the smallest focused Ruby validator/test surface for `validate-implementation-wave.rb`, including a generated Git history fixture that proves `S -> E -> H`, post-source product-drift denial, post-evidence mutation denial, exact-head/merge/ancestry denial, ambiguous/missing mapping denial, fake evidence denial, the full sixteen-child/path/DAG denominator, and #5878 integrated/native receipt preservation.

## Owned scope

- `.csdlc/prepared/issues/5862/validate-implementation-wave.rb`
- Focused validator regression test/fixture paths determined during typed design preparation
- Issue-local C-SDLC lifecycle and evidence paths

## Non-goals

- No closeout rewrite.
- No product or runtime changes.
- No acceptance of unmerged or non-terminal children.
- No weakening of exact path, evidence immutability, ancestry, PR-head, merge, denominator, DAG, or native receipt checks.
- No self-referential proof requirement or hand-authored success bypass.

## Publication boundary

issues.title: [v0.92][runtime-v3] Unify TLS/mTLS and retire self-signed Runtime certificates
issues.body:
## Problem

Runtime TLS is currently split across multiple loaders and trust models. The
HTTP/WSS listeners use Axum with Rustls, Guardian transport uses Quinn with
Rustls, and a production `local_self_signed` bootstrap path generates a
self-signed localhost leaf and mutates the macOS trust store. Runtime init does
not express a complete TLS/mTLS policy, several proofs trust a served leaf as a
root, and application authority credentials are described alongside X.509
transport certificates.

This is the upstream cause of the UnityTLS failure. Installing the existing
self-signed leaf is not an acceptable repair.

## Required outcome

Unify Runtime TLS and mTLS around one maintained Rustls policy and loading
layer:

- Axum is the sole HTTP/HTTPS/WSS server stack.
- Quinn remains the Guardian-to-Guardian QUIC transport.
- Both consume the same certificate, trust, identity, protocol-version, and
  crypto-provider policy types.
- Browser and Unity endpoints use externally provisioned, CA-issued server
  certificates for real DNS names.
- Guardian transport uses externally provisioned private-CA identities and
  standard Rustls mutual authentication.
- Runtime never issues certificates, installs trust roots, disables
  verification, or asks clients to trust a served leaf directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- One shared Runtime TLS module owns declarative identity/trust configuration
  and builds the Rustls configuration consumed by all Axum HTTP/WSS listeners.
- The same trust-policy types are reused by the Quinn Guardian transport
  without replacing Quinn or weakening its TLS 1.3 mutual-authentication
  contract.
- Runtime init explicitly expresses the Axum server identity, trust roots, and
  expected DNS identity. Guardian mTLS remains explicit in Quinn transport
  configuration rather than becoming a browser-facing listener mode.
- Public HTTPS/WSS startup fails closed for a self-signed served leaf, an
  untrusted or incomplete chain, wrong DNS SAN, expiry/not-yet-valid status,
  or unsuitable server-auth usage.
- mTLS admission uses standard Rustls/WebPKI verification with explicit private
  CA roots. Peer identity is available only after a successful handshake; no
  hash constructed before the handshake is described as verified proof.
- `LocalSelfSigned`, production `rcgen` issuance, local certificate reissue,
  macOS trust-install/verify/remove operations, and their ownership receipts
  are removed from Runtime product paths.
- Browser, Unity, operational proof, and documentation surfaces no longer use
  leaf-as-root trust, `curl --cacert <served-leaf>`, verification bypasses, or
  manual host-trust installation.
- Development and production use the same externally provisioned certificate
  path. ACME/Let's Encrypt may provide public certificates for real DNS names;
  Guardian client identities come from an external private CA.
- Certificate rotation is infrastructure-owned. ACM-managed ingress rotates
  outside Runtime; direct Axum termination uses atomic material replacement
  followed by a controlled supervised restart and normal connection drain.
  Runtime does not add a certificate watcher or hot-reload state machine.
- Application-level Guardian authority credentials remain separate from X.509
  TLS identity and are named/documented so they cannot be mistaken for
  transport certificates.
- Runtime and kernel resolve one reviewed Rustls patch level and one crypto
  provider policy.
- Focused tests use a test CA issuing leaf certificates rather than treating a
  self-signed server leaf as trusted. Negative coverage includes self-signed
  leaf, wrong SAN, expired/not-yet-valid, unknown CA, incomplete chain, wrong
  client CA, and missing client identity.
- Unity issue #84 remains gated until a live certificate-valid Axum WSS endpoint
  succeeds without trust-store mutation or certificate-verification bypass.

## Non-goals

- Replacing Quinn with HTTP/2 or adding automatic QUIC fallback.
- Implementing a CA, ACME client, certificate protocol, trust store, or custom
  cryptographic verifier inside ADL.
- Requiring browser or Unity clients to present mTLS certificates.
- Replacing application-level Guardian authorization with transport TLS.

## Review evidence

The contract incorporates independent implementation, security, and
consumer/proof reviews plus Gemini 3.1 Pro review. The reviewers agreed that
the production self-signed bootstrap and host-trust mutation must be removed,
server TLS loading must be unified, and application authority must remain
separate from transport identity. Gemini's suggestion to use `mkcert -install`
was rejected because it would preserve local CA issuance and host-trust
mutation under a different tool.

Supersedes the original #92 managed-external trust-install workaround.
Blocks #84 until terminal validation.

<!-- csdlc-github-operation:v092-issue-92-runtime-tls-standardization-20260809 -->

issues.title: [C-SDLC v2] Add typed STP deliverable correction after review recovery
issues.body:
## Problem

`csdlc-review recover` correctly returns stale reviewed or published work to `implemented`, but `csdlc-edit` cannot then repair a contradictory STP deliverable collection. The implemented-phase allowlist permits STP acceptance correction while rejecting `replace_planning_collection` for STP deliverables. Issue #73 exposed this gap: its STP says fourteen implementation specifications while its acceptance criteria and approved plan require eighteen.

Direct card editing, record deletion/rebootstrap, phase rollback, and an unreviewed one-off binary are forbidden.

## Required Outcome

Add one narrow typed semantic operation, `correct_stp_deliverables_after_recovery`, that can repair STP deliverables only during legitimate post-review recovery and regenerates values and rendered Markdown atomically through the existing store.

## Required Behavior

- Accept issue, expected generation/digest, actor, reason, and a nonempty replacement deliverable list.
- Permit the operation only for card `stp` in phase `implemented`.
- Require review assignment, review result, publication, readiness, and terminal truth to be cleared by typed recovery.
- Reject blank or duplicate deliverables.
- Preserve issue scope and every other STP field.
- Record previous and replacement values in durable audit evidence.
- Regenerate typed values, rendered Markdown, AST digest, and record digest atomically.
- Reject wrong card, every other phase, stale CAS, stale design/projection state, and malformed replacement input.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A recovered implemented issue can correct only its STP deliverables through `csdlc-edit apply`.
2. An implemented issue that has not passed through review recovery cannot use the operation.
3. Reviewed, published, bound, merge-ready, merged, and closed-out issues reject it.
4. Wrong-card, stale-CAS, blank, duplicate, and projection-drift requests fail closed.
5. Audit evidence records actor, reason, previous values, and replacements.
6. Focused Rust tests, formatting, and strict Clippy pass.
7. Issue #73 can consume the installed operation to replace fourteen with eighteen without hand-editing its cards.

## Scope

- `csdlc-v2/src/cards.rs`
- `csdlc-v2/src/store.rs`
- focused C-SDLC v2 tests and generated schema assertions
- typed lifecycle cards and proof for this issue

## Non-Goals

- General post-implementation STP editing.
- Phase rollback from implemented to bound.
- Direct Markdown or JSON mutation.
- Changing issue #73's architecture or implementing C-SDLC v3.
- Weakening exact review, publication, CAS, projection, or lifecycle gates.

issues.title: C-SDLC v2 publish cannot represent non-closing incremental parent checkpoints
issues.body:
## Problem

`csdlc-publish publish` rejects every publication request that lacks a GitHub closing keyword for the tracked issue. That makes the typed publication path unusable for an intentionally incremental checkpoint PR that must leave its parent issue open and use `Part of owner/repo#issue`.

Observed while remediating PR #69 for legacy WP-24A issue danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5845. Episode 001 is a complete bounded checkpoint, but the parent owns ten episodes and must remain open.

## Current behavior

`prepare_publication` requires `body_has_github_closing_keyword` (or the qualified split-repository equivalent), so a truthful non-closing checkpoint cannot pass typed publication.

## Required behavior

- Add an explicit typed publication linkage mode such as `closing` or `part_of`.
- Require qualified linkage for split issue/code repositories in either mode.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior: `part_of` must never silently close the issue.
- Record the selected linkage mode in publication evidence.
- Add positive and negative tests for same-repository and split-repository incremental checkpoints.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A typed `part_of` publication can create or update a PR without a closing keyword.
2. The PR body must contain the exact qualified `Part of owner/repo#issue` relation for split authority.
3. Closing publication behavior remains unchanged.
4. Publication evidence and reconciliation distinguish closing from non-closing linkage.
5. Focused Rust tests cover invalid/missing/ambiguous linkage.

issues.title: [v0.92][Provider] Add first-class Deepgram speech provider
issues.body:
## Context

WP-24A proved that Deepgram Aura-2 can provide a materially better and more distinct surrogate voice for Claude in the Cognitive Spacetime podcast. The current podcast renderer calls Deepgram directly. ADL should expose this capability through a reusable, typed provider boundary instead of leaving each workflow to implement authentication, requests, outputs, and evidence independently.

## Goal

Add a first-class Deepgram speech provider that follows the existing ADL provider architecture and supports deterministic, governed batch speech operations.

## Required outcome

ADL can perform batch text-to-speech and speech-to-text through Deepgram using typed requests and results, redacted configuration, stable artifact metadata, explicit provider identity, and focused offline plus bounded live validation.

## Scope

- Define typed Deepgram configuration, capability, request, response, and error contracts.
- Integrate the provider through the existing provider/profile boundary rather than a podcast-specific abstraction.
- Support batch text-to-speech with explicit model, voice, encoding, sample rate, and container selection.
- Support batch prerecorded-audio transcription with explicit model and language configuration.
- Preserve transcript author, audio renderer, model, voice, media properties, request identity, timing, and usage metadata without retaining credentials.
- Resolve credentials from an explicit environment variable or operator-approved key file without printing or persisting secret values.
- Provide deterministic mock transport tests and a separately gated live canary using a minimal fixture.
- Document provider setup and one small reusable example for downstream workflows such as Podcast Studio.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deepgram is registered through the canonical ADL provider/profile mechanism with typed capability discovery.
- [ ] Typed batch synthesis accepts text plus explicit voice/media settings and returns validated audio bytes plus redacted provenance metadata.
- [ ] Typed batch transcription accepts a declared audio artifact and returns a structured transcript plus redacted provenance metadata.
- [ ] Provider errors distinguish authentication, throttling, invalid input, unsupported media, timeout, transport, and malformed response failures.
- [ ] No API key or authorization header appears in logs, errors, manifests, fixtures, or retained evidence.
- [ ] Deterministic tests cover request construction, response parsing, media validation, redaction, timeout, malformed responses, and provider errors without network access.
- [ ] One opt-in bounded live canary proves synthesis and transcription against current Deepgram APIs and records cost, latency, model identity, media properties, and redacted request identity.
- [ ] Podcast Studio can consume the provider without embedding Deepgram HTTP or credential logic in the episode workflow.
- [ ] Focused documentation explains configuration, supported operations, evidence boundaries, and current limitations.
- [ ] Independent exact-head review has no unresolved actionable findings.

## Validation

- Focused Rust tests for the provider and HTTP adapter.
- Credential and log redaction checks.
- Audio container and media-property validation against deterministic fixtures.
- Opt-in minimal live synthesis and transcription round trip using operator-provided credentials.
- Diff hygiene and bounded exact-head review.

## Non-goals

- Migrating or rerendering Episode 001.
- Real-time conversational orchestration or Gemini Live integration.
- Voice cloning, custom voice training, or biometric identity claims.
- A general media editor or mastering engine.
- Automatic provider selection based only on price.
- Broad refactoring of the existing provider subsystem.

issues.title: C-SDLC editor cannot correct SIP scope after implemented review finding

issues.title: C-SDLC bind topology scan misresolves historical worktree dot records
issues.body:
## Problem

`csdlc-bind` scans every issue record in every listed worktree. Historical records with `worktree: "."` are resolved relative to the worktree being scanned, so each such record appears to own the currently requested worktree. The scan then fully verifies unrelated historical cards and may fail with raw `ENOENT` when an old record references intentionally untracked local design artifacts.

Observed while binding issue #53 at current main `170a25a160a2c6fe9f456fb59ac27eb5e0c34740`: the scan treated historical #5791 as relevant because its stored worktree is `.`, then `verify_cards` tried to read absent `.adl/local-artifacts/5791-bootstrap/design.md` and returned `No such file or directory (os error 2)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Relative stored worktree paths are resolved against their recorded/canonical repository topology, not whichever worktree is currently being scanned.
- An unrelated historical record with `worktree: "."` cannot collide with a new issue-local bind.
- Topology scanning does not require absent authored artifacts for records proven irrelevant by issue, branch, and canonical worktree identity.
- A regression reproduces #5791-style `worktree: "."` plus absent local authored artifacts and proves a distinct issue binds successfully.
- Genuine same-issue, same-branch, or same-canonical-worktree collisions still fail closed with a typed reconciliation error.
- Raw filesystem errors identify the affected issue/path when they remain possible.

## Non-goals

- Do not mutate retained #5791 evidence.
- Do not weaken card verification for a genuinely relevant topology record.
- Do not widen issue #53's execution-proof receipt scope.

issues.title: [v0.92][Codex goals] Allow replacing a blocked goal when work is redirected
issues.body:
## Problem

A thread whose previous goal is terminally `blocked` cannot create a new issue-bound goal. `create_goal` returns `cannot create a new goal because this thread has an unfinished goal`, even after the operator explicitly redirects the thread to a different sprint and issue.

## Reproduction

1. Create a goal.
2. Mark it `blocked` through the goal API.
3. Redirect the thread to a different tracked issue.
4. Call `create_goal` for the new issue.
5. Observe that creation is rejected as an unfinished-goal conflict.

## Impact

ADL policy requires an issue-bound session goal before implementation. The stale blocked goal therefore prevents legitimate work from starting and cannot be resolved truthfully: marking the old objective complete would be false, while marking it blocked again changes nothing.

## Expected Behavior

A terminal blocked goal can be explicitly replaced after operator redirection, while preserving its historical status and accounting. Alternatively, expose a typed abandon/supersede transition that records the replacement objective.

## Evidence

The current thread goal is blocked with the Sprint #5862 objective. Attempting to create the Sprint #5855 child #5795 goal failed with the unfinished-goal error. The #5795 worktree was bound successfully, but no implementation edits were started.

issues.title: C-SDLC v2 execution-proof receipts cannot bind a committed evidence head without self-reference
issues.body:
## Problem

The WP-04.01 execution-proof validator requires `source.revision` to equal the current Git HEAD while the receipt itself is a tracked artifact. A valid receipt generated against substantive head A can only be committed at later head B; changing the receipt to B creates another later commit C. This makes exact-current-HEAD committed receipts self-referential and impossible to satisfy without treating the evidence commit separately.

Observed on legacy issue danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5863:
- substantive implementation/proof head: `18651760fae886bcd9db4b8d4e883c7ab02be601`
- evidence-only commit: `9cb7fbe1961539e8b62f3093d023c9aa367df4b8`
- the focused proof validator passes when the receipt truthfully binds the substantive source revision, but a review correctly flags that the repository HEAD is the later evidence commit.

## Required behavior

Define and enforce a non-self-referential contract, for example by binding receipts to an explicit substantive revision plus evidence-commit ancestry, or by excluding evidence-only commits from the source-revision equality rule while retaining tamper-evident artifact digests.

## Acceptance criteria

- A tracked execution-proof receipt can be committed without requiring an infinite sequence of HEAD rewrites.
- The validator distinguishes substantive source revision from evidence-only commit revision.
- Both revisions and their ancestry are machine-verified.
- Tampering with source, test, logs, or receipt still fails closed.
- Focused regression covers substantive commit A followed by evidence-only commit B.

## Non-goal

Do not weaken exact-revision or artifact-digest verification.

issues.title: Native receipt validator has an impossible artifact-role denominator
issues.body:
## Problem

The WP-03 native receipt validator sorts observed artifact roles but compares them to an unsorted canonical role list. Every otherwise valid macOS/Linux receipt therefore fails with `artifact role denominator drift`.

The validator also needs an explicit, fail-closed distinction between the exact tested product revision and a later verifier-only repair; otherwise fixing the verifier itself forces expensive product soak reruns despite no product-byte change.

## Acceptance

- Compare canonical and observed role denominators order-independently.
- Keep role uniqueness enforced.
- Permit post-proof changes only to an explicit verifier-only allowlist, verified from Git.
- Reject any runtime/product change after the proof revision.
- Preserve digest recomputation and platform denominator checks.

## Acceptance

- No process-substitution dependency in the paid execution path.
- stdout/stderr are retained separately.
- manager exit status remains authoritative.
- existing redaction/finalization behavior remains intact.
- focused shell regression passes.
