issues.body:
## Summary

The canonical CI workflow launches both full-workspace coverage producer shards even when path policy explicitly classifies workspace coverage as not required. This defeats the WP-02A lane-selection objective, adds roughly 25 minutes to a Runtime-local PR, and consumes unnecessary hosted-runner resources.

Observed on canonical PR #9 / Actions run 31143017130:

- `adl-coverage-runtime-hosted` was the relevant coverage lane and passed.
- `adl-coverage-workspace-hosted (1/2)` and `(2/2)` each reported `Coverage not required by path policy`.
- Despite that classification, both jobs proceeded into `Workspace coverage run and summary (json)`.
- Branch protection then waited for the downstream `adl-coverage` aggregation, preventing merge even though `adl-ci`, Runtime coverage, Rust tests, lint, tooling contracts, demo proof, and slow-proof lanes were green.

## Required Outcome

Path policy must prevent optional coverage producer jobs from launching expensive setup or coverage execution when their lane is not required. Required aggregate checks must still conclude deterministically and successfully from explicit skipped/not-required evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Runtime-local change that does not require full-workspace coverage does not execute either workspace coverage shard.
- Job-level `if` routing occurs before Rust/tool installation and coverage execution, not inside the expensive step.
- The required `adl-coverage` check still reaches a terminal success result when workspace coverage is intentionally skipped.
- Runtime coverage still runs when selected.
- Full-workspace coverage still runs when path policy selects it.
- Focused contract tests cover selected and unselected producer/aggregator combinations.
- Retained timing evidence shows optional producers consume no hosted execution time beyond GitHub skipped-job accounting.

## Non-Goals

- Changing coverage thresholds.
- Weakening required coverage when policy selects it.
- Modifying Runtime TLS issue #5800.

## Evidence

Canonical PR: https://github.com/agent-logic/agent-design-language/pull/9
Actions run: https://github.com/agent-logic/agent-design-language/actions/runs/31143017130

This issue belongs only in the canonical Agent Logic repository.

issues.title: [v0.92][repository migration] Migrate the ADL issue tracker to the canonical Agent Logic repository
issues.body:
## Outcome

Migrate ADL issue authority from `danielbaustin/agent-design-language` to `agent-logic/agent-design-language` so all continuing work is planned, implemented, reviewed, published, and closed in the canonical repository. The migration must account for every legacy issue and leave no active issue dependent on the personal repository.

This is the repository issue-tracker migration. It is separate from canonical issue #3, which only adds compatibility for canonical PRs closing preserved legacy issues.

## Required scope

1. Produce a complete, machine-readable census of every legacy issue, including open, closed, transferred, duplicate, superseded, PR-linked, milestone-bound, project-linked, and C-SDLC-bound states.
2. Define and prove the GitHub-supported transfer path, permission requirements, identity changes, comment/event continuity, labels, milestones, assignees, projects, dependencies, links, and automation effects.
3. Transfer every issue GitHub permits into `agent-logic/agent-design-language`, preserving history and recording the old and new identities.
4. Ensure no open or continuing ADL issue remains authoritative in `danielbaustin/agent-design-language`. Any GitHub state that cannot be transferred must receive an explicit, reviewed preservation and canonical-successor disposition; it may not disappear from the census.
5. Migrate C-SDLC issue identity, cards, evidence, branch/worktree bindings, publication/review/readiness/finish truth, sprint packets, milestone plans, dependency edges, and durable references without overwriting same-number canonical issues or inventing completion.
6. Use repository-qualified issue identity during migration and preserve a durable old-to-new mapping for every issue. Number-only identity is not sufficient.
7. Update canonical operator tooling, schemas, docs, issue links, and automation so new issues and all future lifecycle work target only `agent-logic/agent-design-language`.
8. Prove canonical GitHub issue reads/writes, PR closing relationships, CI links, milestone/project continuity, and terminal closeout after migration.
9. Keep the legacy repository public and historical; do not delete, privatize, rewrite, or force-push it.
10. Execute through staged canaries, reviewed batches, reconciliation checkpoints, and a final zero-active-legacy-issue audit.

## Acceptance criteria

- A signed census and migration ledger dispositions every legacy issue exactly once.
- Every active issue has canonical issue authority and a verified canonical lifecycle binding.
- Every transferred issue has observed source and destination identity, preserved history, and reconciled metadata.
- Same-number collisions are detected and resolved without overwrite or ambiguity.
- C-SDLC records and evidence resolve through repository-qualified identity and retain audit continuity.
- Milestones, dependencies, sprint membership, PR links, closing references, and automation are reconciled against live canonical state.
- New issue creation and lifecycle defaults cannot target the legacy repository.
- The migration is restartable, idempotent, fail-closed, and recoverable without destructive rollback.
- Architecture, security, Claude, Gemini, and human exact-head reviews have no unresolved blocker or high-severity finding.
- Final proof shows zero active ADL issues remain authoritative in the legacy repository and no required issue was omitted.

## Non-goals

- Deleting or rewriting legacy repository history.
- Moving unrelated repositories or non-ADL issue trackers.
- Using AWS or remote builders.
- Treating issue recreation without preserved mapping and reviewed disposition as equivalent to transfer.
- Silently closing, duplicating, or dropping issues to make counts converge.

issues.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC v2] Support canonical PRs closing preserved legacy issues
issues.body:
## Outcome

Allow typed C-SDLC v2 publication to create and reconcile a pull request in the canonical `agent-logic/agent-design-language` code repository while closing an existing issue retained on `danielbaustin/agent-design-language` with a qualified GitHub closing reference.

This is the publication migration blocker discovered by WP-24 issue `danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5844`. No additional mutation of the preserved legacy code repository is authorized.

## Observed evidence

- Canonical code and push authority is `agent-logic/agent-design-language`; shared `origin` points there.
- Existing v0.92 issue authority remains on `danielbaustin/agent-design-language`.
- The cutover contract requires canonical pull requests with qualified closure text such as `Closes danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5844`.
- `PublicationRequest` currently has one `repository` identity.
- `csdlc-publish` requires that identity to match the typed issue record, Git remote URL, queried/observed pull-request repository, and closing-keyword repository.
- A canonical request therefore fails typed record matching, while a legacy request targets the prohibited legacy code repository.
- WP-24 retained the exact evidence in `.csdlc/evidence/5844/CANONICAL_PUBLICATION_IDENTITY_BLOCKER.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Typed publication represents the canonical code/PR repository separately from the preserved issue-tracker repository and issue number.
2. The Git remote, observed base/head repositories, pushed branch, and created/reconciled PR must match the canonical code repository exactly.
3. The PR body must contain a valid qualified closing keyword for the preserved tracker issue, such as `Closes danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5844`.
4. Same-repository publication remains backward compatible and fail-closed.
5. Cross-repository publication rejects unqualified issue references, mismatched tracker identity, fork/base/head drift, ambiguous PR matches, stale exact-head review, and legacy code-repository pushes.
6. Public request schemas, tests, operator skill documentation, publication evidence, readiness, and finish/closeout validation cover both identities.
7. A focused canary proves a canonical Agent Logic PR can close a preserved legacy issue without mutating legacy repository code, refs, settings, or pull requests.

## Non-goals

- Moving or renumbering existing legacy issues.
- Rewriting historical lifecycle records.
- Closing or modifying the erroneous legacy WP-24 PR.
- Weakening exact repository, revision, review, linkage, or remote-state verification.
- Enabling AWS workflows or changing unrelated CI policy.

<!-- csdlc-github-operation:wp24-cross-repository-publication-identity-20260807 -->
